literature.headline_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期乙型肝炎病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 在多个印度州中,HBV基因型D(70.96%)是最常见的基因型,基因型A(3.22%)存在于中部和南部州,基因型C(6.45%)则分布在东北部。值得注意的是,有五份样本显示出重组事件的证据,包括基因型A、C和D。对代表性分离株的SimPlot分析清楚地显示了重组断点。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10773367/v1]
作者强调了三个方面的早期但有希望的结果:利用机器学习进行图像的定量分析、通过多模态模型整合临床和病理数据,以及基于连续测量进行治疗反应的动态预测。 [10.3748/wjg.120151]
三次剂量后,6个月治疗后,高达90%的动物检测不到乙型肝炎表面抗原和HBV DNA。 [10.1038/s41551-026-01802-8]
在426名参与者中,167人(39.2%)至少接种过一剂HBV疫苗,38.5%的人完成了疫苗接种系列。在双变量分析中,疫苗接种与教育程度、职业、居住类型、选区、宗教信仰、HBV知识和医疗工作者推荐显著相关(所有p值均<0.05). [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10643855/v1]
在乙型肝炎病毒表面抗原(S基因)中,突变的整体检出率为55.0%,BCP 突变为28.3%,PreCore 突变为66.7%,在60个分析的基因组全基因组序列中,Core和X基因中的突变均被检测到。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10993872/v1]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: HBV genotype D (70.96%) was found to be common genotype in several Indian states, with genotype A (3.22%) present in central and southern states and genotype C (6.45%) in the northeast. Notably, five samples showed evidence of recombination events, including genotypes A, C, and D. [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10773367/v1]

The authors highlight early but encouraging results from three areas: quantitative image analysis using ML, multimodal integration of clinical and pathological data, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements. [10.3748/wjg.120151]
Three doses resulted in up to 90% of animals with undetectable hepatitis B surface antigen and HBV DNA by 6 months post treatment. [10.1038/s41551-026-01802-8]

Among 426 participants, 167 (39.2%) had received at least one dose of HBV vaccine, and 38.5% had completed the vaccination series. In bivariate analyses, vaccine uptake was significantly associated with education, occupation, residence type, ward, religion, HBV knowledge, and health worker recommendation (all p. [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10643855/v1]

The overall detection rate of mutations in the hepatitis B virus surface antigen (S gene) was 55.0%, BCP mutations – 28.3%, PreCore mutations – 66.7%, and mutations in the Core and X genes were detected in each of the 60 analyzed genome-wide sequences of HBV variants. [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10993872/v1]

news.headline_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期乙型肝炎病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 事件是制定欧洲产前筛查艾滋病、乙型肝炎和梅毒的标准,包括垂直传播率的数据。该报告由欧洲疾病预防控制中心(ECDC)和欧洲艾滋病临床学会(EACS)发布。 [news-ff5c7963ab892511]
印度重申了到2030年消除乙型肝炎和丙型肝炎作为公共卫生威胁的承诺,正如联合卫生部长Punya Salila Srivastava在联合国大会边会上所强调的(N2)。这是一个确认的承诺,而不是暴发或事件(N1)。 [news-dbaa40d0f17b7c1e]
Xia & He Publishing Inc.发表的一项研究突出了乙型肝炎病毒基因型C的高风险表型的分子基础及其临床意义,强调其与延迟HBeAg血清转换、持续病毒复制、活跃的炎症反应、更快的纤维化进展以及更高的肝细胞癌(HCC)风险相关。 [news-37faf7a240295c3b]
推荐了一种新的慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)治疗策略,将重点从肝酶水平转移到病毒载量,特别是HBV DNA水平,以确定抗病毒治疗(治疗)的适用性。 [news-6544acb7ea6e4bf6]
一位患有慢性乙型肝炎的女性停用了抗病毒药物药物并服用草药,导致肝功能恶化并最终死亡。韩国医疗纠纷调解与仲裁机构审查了此案,并得出结论,认为诊所未能充分履行解释和监测停药及使用草药相关风险的责任。 [news-e6de4d116c7a3b15]

news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Hepatitis B virus news developments.
key_findings_en: The event is the development of European standards for antenatal screening for HIV, hepatitis B, and syphilis, including data on vertical transmission rates. The report is published by the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) and the European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS). [news-ff5c7963ab892511]

India has reaffirmed its commitment to eliminating Hepatitis B and C as public health threats by 2030, as stated by the Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava during a side event of the UN General Assembly (N2). This is a confirmed commitment, not an outbreak or incident (N1). [news-dbaa40d0f17b7c1e]
A study published by Xia & He Publishing Inc. [news-37faf7a240295c3b]

A new treatment strategy for chronic hepatitis B has been recommended, shifting focus from liver enzyme levels to viral load, particularly HBV DNA levels, for determining antiviral treatment. [news-6544acb7ea6e4bf6]
A woman with chronic hepatitis B stopped her antiviral medication and took herbal medicine, leading to a deterioration in her liver function and eventual death. [news-e6de4d116c7a3b15]

papers.title: Long-term stability and reproducibility of frozen plasma control samples for hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, and human immunodeficiency virus by quantitative PCR: Implications for retrospective testing in hemovigilance.
papers.abstract: Abstract Objective Data on the long‐term stability and reproducibility of nucleic acid amplification testing (NAT) results in frozen stored positive samples (≤−20°C) remain limited. This study evaluated the long‐term performance of frozen virus‐positive samples in quantitative PCR assays and aimed to provide evidence for their analytical reliability in retrospective NAT and quality assurance. Because blood transfusions, despite their high safety, still carry a residual risk of transmission of blood‐borne viruses, these data may also be relevant for look‐back investigations in hemovigilance. Materials and Methods Diluted and aliquoted internal run controls from positive patient samples were retrospectively analyzed using routine quantitative PCR assays. Long‐term stability was assessed over 37 months for HIV, 25 and 29 months for HBV‐A and HBV‐B, and 49 and 38 months for HCV‐A and HCV‐B. Descriptive statistics and linear regression were used to assess variability and temporal trends. Compliance with the German Medical Association's guidelines for quality assurance in medical laboratory testing (Rili‐BAEK) was evaluated using an acceptance range of ±0.5 log10. Results All internal run controls demonstrated stable long‐term performance during frozen storage and routine use. Across the datasets, 99.2%–100% of measurements remained within the acceptance range. Results outside mean ± 3 SD were rare, and no statistically significant temporal trend was observed for any internal run control. Conclusion Frozen HBV‐, HCV‐, and HIV‐positive samples showed robust long‐term stability and reproducibility in routine quantitative PCR assays for up to 4 years. These findings support the suitability of long‐term stored specimens for retrospective NAT.

elements_en.main_results: All internal run controls demonstrated stable long-term performance during frozen storage and routine use, with 99.2%–100% of measurements remaining within the acceptance range, and no statistically significant temporal trend was observed.

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现对输血安全监测中的回顾性调查具有相关性,并支持长期保存的样本用于回顾性NAT,从而提高血液输注的安全性。

papers.title_zh: 冷冻血浆控制样本在乙型肝炎病毒、丙型肝炎病毒和人类免疫缺陷病毒定量PCR检测中的长期稳定性和可重复性:对输血安全监测中回顾性检测的启示。
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Objective Data on the long‐term stability and reproducibility of nucleic acid amplification testing (NAT) results in frozen stored positive samples (≤−20°C) remain limited. This study evaluated the long‐term performance of frozen virus‐positive samples in quantitative PCR assays and aimed to provide evidence for their analytical reliability in retrospective NAT and quality assurance. Because blood transfusions, despite their high safety, still carry a residual risk of transmission of blood‐borne viruses, these data may also be relevant for look‐back investigations in hemovigilance. Materials and Methods Diluted and aliquoted internal run controls from positive patient samples were retrospectively analyzed using routine quantitative PCR assays. Long‐term stability was assessed over 37 months for HIV, 25 and 29 months for HBV‐A and HBV‐B, and 49 and 38 months for HCV‐A and HCV‐B. Descriptive statistics and linear regression were used to assess variability and temporal trends. Compliance with the German Medical Association's guidelines for quality assurance in medical laboratory testing (Rili‐BAEK) was evaluated using an acceptance range of ±0.5 log10. Results All internal run controls demonstrated stable long‐term performance during frozen storage and routine use. Across the datasets, 99.2%–100% of measurements remained within the acceptance range. Results outside mean ± 3 SD were rare, and no statistically significant temporal trend was observed for any internal run control. Conclusion Frozen HBV‐, HCV‐, and HIV‐positive samples showed robust long‐term stability and reproducibility in routine quantitative PCR assays for up to 4 years. These findings support the suitability of long‐term stored specimens for retrospective NAT.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 目的 目前关于冷冻保存的阳性样本(≤−20°C)中核酸扩增检测(NAT)结果的长期稳定性和可重复性数据仍然有限。本研究评估了冷冻保存的病毒阳性样本在定量PCR检测中的长期性能,并旨在为其在回顾性NAT和质量保证中的分析可靠性提供证据。尽管血液输注具有较高的安全性,但仍存在血液传播病毒传播的残留风险,因此这些数据也可能对输血安全监测中的回顾性调查具有相关性。材料和方法 使用来自阳性患者样本的稀释和分装的内部运行控制样本,通过常规的定量PCR检测进行回顾性分析。长期稳定性评估分别在HIV样本上进行了37个月,在HBV-A和HBV-B样本上进行了25和29个月,在HCV-A和HCV-B样本上进行了49和38个月。使用描述性统计和线性回归来评估变异性和时间趋势。通过德国医学协会关于医疗实验室检测质量保证的指南(Rili-BAEK)的接受范围±0.5 log10来评估符合情况。结果 所有内部运行控制样本在冷冻保存和常规使用过程中均表现出稳定的长期性能。在所有数据集中,99.2%–100%的测量值均保持在接受范围内。测量值超出均值±3 SD的情况很少,且任何内部运行控制样本均未观察到统计学上显著的时间趋势。结论 冷冻保存的HBV、HCV和HIV阳性样本在常规定量PCR检测中表现出良好的长期稳定性和可重复性,最长可达4年。这些发现支持长期保存的样本用于回顾性NAT的适用性。

papers.title: Associated factors of hepatitis B virus infection among pregnant women in Africa: an extension of a previous systematic review and meta-analysis on prevalence
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a significant public health concern among pregnant women in Africa. While previous reviews have focused on the prevalence of HBV, comprehensive evidence regarding the associated factors of HBV infection is limited. Therefore, this systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to identify the associated factors of HBV infection in pregnant women in Africa. We systematically searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Advanced Google Scholar, the Cochrane Library, and African Journal Online for observational studies published between July 18, 2013, and July 18, 2023. Studies reporting adjusted effect estimates for factors associated with HBV infection among pregnant women were included. We assessed methodological quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS). We conducted separate random-effects meta-analyses using the DerSimonian–Laird method for each associated factor reported by at least two studies to estimate pooled adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Associated factors examined across multiple studies that differed substantially in exposure categories or reference groups were synthesized narratively. Statistical heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic. Of the 19 included studies, 20 associated factors were eligible for the quantitative synthesis. Significant associations with HBV infection among pregnant women were a history of abortion (AOR = 3.08, 95% CI: 1.58–4.58), multiple sexual partners (AOR = 5.33, 95% CI: 2.50–8.17), blood transfusion (AOR = 2.64, 95% CI: 1.38–3.90), hospital admission (AOR = 3.28, 95% CI: 2.02–4.53), surgery (AOR = 2.48, 95% CI: 1.04–3.92), HIV infection (AOR = 9.22, 95% CI: 2.39–16.05), tattooing (AOR = 2.53, 95% CI: 1.26–3.80), female genital mutilation (AOR = 2.48, 95% CI: 2.02–2.94), dental procedures (AOR = 2.30, 95% CI: 1.16–3,44), family history of HBV infection (AOR = 3.37, 95% CI: 1.94–4.80), contact with jaundiced patients (AOR = 4.18, 95% CI: 2.09–6.27), tonsillectomy (AOR = 4.87, 95% CI: 3.36–6.37), and sharing sharp materials (AOR = 2.87, 95% CI: 2.47–3.27). This meta-analysis identified multiple behavioral, medical, and household-related associated factors of HBV infection. Strengthening routine antenatal HBV screening, targeted risk assessment, vaccination strategies, and linkage-to-care interventions may help improve early detection and reduce mother-to-child transmission of HBV. PROSPERO 2025 CRD420251240694.

We conducted separate random-effects meta-analyses using the DerSimonian–Laird method for each associated factor reported by at least two studies to estimate pooled adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Associated factors examined across multiple studies that differed substantially in exposure categories or reference groups were synthesized narratively. Statistical heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic. Of the 19 included studies, 20 associated factors were eligible for the quantitative synthesis. Significant associations with HBV infection among pregnant women were a history of abortion (AOR = 3.08, 95% CI: 1.58–4.58), multiple sexual partners (AOR = 5.33, 95% CI: 2.50–8.17), blood transfusion (AOR = 2.64, 95% CI: 1.38–3.90), hospital admission (AOR = 3.28, 95% CI: 2.02–4.53), surgery (AOR = 2.48, 95% CI: 1.04–3.92), HIV infection (AOR = 9.22, 95% CI: 2.39–16.05), tattooing (AOR = 2.53, 95% CI: 1.26–3.80), female genital mutilation (AOR = 2.48, 95% CI: 2.02–2.94), dental procedures (AOR = 2.30, 95% CI: 1.16–3,44), family history of HBV infection (AOR = 3.37, 95% CI: 1.94–4.80), contact with jaundiced patients (AOR = 4.18, 95% CI: 2.09–6.27), tonsillectomy (AOR = 4.87, 95% CI: 3.36–6.37), and sharing sharp materials (AOR = 2.87, 95% CI: 2.47–3.27). This meta-analysis identified multiple behavioral, medical, and household-related associated factors of HBV infection. Strengthening routine antenatal HBV screening, targeted risk assessment, vaccination strategies, and linkage-to-care interventions may help improve early detection and reduce mother-to-child transmission of HBV. papers.title: Hepatitis B Virus Knowledge, Preventive Practices, and Vaccination Status Among People Living with HIV at the Nigerian Institute of Medical Research, Lagos: A Cross-Sectional Study
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) co-infection substantially increases liver-related morbidity and mortality among people living with HIV (PLHIV). Although vaccination remains the most effective strategy for prevention HBV infection, its uptake is conventionally assumed to depend on adequate knowledge and positive attitudes towards vaccination. This study assessed knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding HBV vaccination among HIV-positive patients and examined whether knowledge significantly predicts vaccination uptake. A cross-sectional institutional survey was conducted among 374 HIV-positive patients receiving care at the Nigerian Institute of Medical Research (NIMR), Yaba, Lagos State. Participants were selected using purposive sampling. and data were collected using a structured questionnaire. Data were analysed using SPSS version 26.0, through descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and logistic regression with statistical significance set at p<0.05. The majority of respondents were female (70.2%), married (62.9%), and had tertiary-educated (40.7%). Overall, 82% of participants demonstrated low levels of knowledge regarding HBV infection and vaccination (Mean=1.20±0.443), while 58% exhibited negative attitudes toward HBV vaccination (Mean=2.73±0.580). Despite these findings, self-reported HBV vaccination uptake was relatively high (79.6%, Mean = 1.4\11±0.423). Healthcare facilities were identified as the primary source of HBV related information. Education level were significantly associated with vaccination status (p=0.025), while gender was significantly associated with knowledge level (p = 0.010). Occupation was not significantly associated with attitude (p = 0.466). Logistic regression analysis indicated that knowledge was not a significant predictor of vaccination uptake (χ2 = 4.49, p = 0.106, R2 = 0.018). The findings demonstrate a notable disconnect between knowledge and predominantly negative attitudes. This challenge the conventional assumption that knowledge necessarily drives vaccination behavior and suggest that health-system factors, including routine vaccine provision and health-care provider recommendations, may play a more important role in vaccination uptake among PLHIV. Interventions should therefore combine improved vaccine accessibility and provider-led vaccination strategies with targeted education, particularly through the integration of HBV vaccination into routine HIV care.

Overall, 82% of participants demonstrated low levels of knowledge regarding HBV infection and vaccination (Mean=1.20±0.443), while 58% exhibited negative attitudes toward HBV vaccination (Mean=2.73±0.580). Despite these findings, self-reported HBV vaccination uptake was relatively high (79.6%, Mean = 1.4\11±0.423). Healthcare facilities were identified as the primary source of HBV related information. Education level were significantly associated with vaccination status (p=0.025), while gender was significantly associated with knowledge level (p = 0.010). Occupation was not significantly associated with attitude (p = 0.466). Logistic regression analysis indicated that knowledge was not a significant predictor of vaccination uptake (χ2 = 4.49, p = 0.106, R2 = 0.018). The findings demonstrate a notable disconnect between knowledge and predominantly negative attitudes. This challenge the conventional assumption that knowledge necessarily drives vaccination behavior and suggest that health-system factors, including routine vaccine provision and health-care provider recommendations, may play a more important role in vaccination uptake among PLHIV. Interventions should therefore combine improved vaccine accessibility and provider-led vaccination strategies with targeted education, particularly through the integration of HBV vaccination into routine HIV care.

papers.abstract_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)共感染显著增加了HIV携带者(PLHIV)的肝相关发病率和死亡率。尽管疫苗接种仍然是预防HBV感染最有效的策略,但其普及率通常被认为取决于对疫苗接种的充分知识和积极态度。本研究评估了HIV阳性患者对HBV疫苗接种的知识、态度和行为,并探讨了知识是否显著预测疫苗接种的普及率。在尼日利亚医学研究所(NIMR)位于拉各斯州亚巴的机构中,对374名接受HIV治疗的患者进行了横断面调查。参与者通过目的抽样法选取,数据通过结构化问卷收集。数据使用SPSS 26.0版本进行分析,包括描述性统计、卡方检验和逻辑回归分析,统计学显著性设定为p<0.05。大多数受访者为女性(70.2%),已婚(62.9%),拥有高等教育背景(40.7%)。总体而言,82%的参与者对HBV感染和疫苗接种的知识水平较低(均值=1.20±0.443),而58%的受访者对HBV疫苗接种表现出负面态度(均值=2.73±0.580)。尽管如此,自我报告的HBV疫苗接种普及率相对较高(79.6%,均值=1.4\11±0.423)。医疗设施被确认为HBV相关信息的主要来源。教育水平与疫苗接种状态显著相关(p=0.025),而性别与知识水平显著相关(p=0.010)。职业与态度无显著相关性(p=0.466)。逻辑回归分析表明,知识不是疫苗接种普及率的显著预测因素(χ2=4.49,p=0.106,R2=0.018)。研究结果表明,知识与主要负面态度之间存在显著脱节。这挑战了传统假设,即知识必然驱动疫苗接种行为,并表明健康系统因素,包括常规抗病毒药物的提供和医疗保健提供者的建议,可能在HIV携带者中对疫苗接种普及率发挥更重要的作用。因此,干预措施应结合改善抗病毒药物的可及性、以医疗保健提供者为主导的疫苗接种策略以及有针对性的教育,特别是在将HBV疫苗接种纳入常规HIV护理中时。

papers.title: Realizing personalized prediction for the reversal of chronic hepatitis B-associated liver fibrosis through machine learning
papers.abstract: Although long-term antiviral therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in a considerable proportion of patients with chronic hepatitis B, treatment response differs markedly among individuals, and reliable methods for predicting who will benefit remain lacking. Conventional clinical tools such as liver stiffness measurement and the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index were originally dewsigned for cross-sectional staging rather than longitudinal prediction, and their ability to capture the dynamic process of fibrosis reversal is limited. In this opinion review, we discuss how machine learning (ML) may help address this unmet need. We focus on three areas where ML has shown early but encouraging results: Quantitative analysis of images using ML, integration of pathological and clinical data through multimodal models, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy. In our view, the greatest value of ML lies not in replacing existing assessment tools but in complementing them, particularly through the early identification of patients who are unlikely to achieve fibrosis reversal with antiviral therapy alone. However, we also caution that most current models have been developed from small, single-center retrospective cohorts, and their clinical adoption will require prospective multi-center validation, improved model interpretability, and adherence to standardized reporting frameworks.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of reliable methods for predicting individual treatment response to antiviral therapy in chronic hepatitis B patients, as long-term therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in some individuals but not all.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This opinion review discusses the potential of machine learning to improve prediction of fibrosis reversal in chronic hepatitis B, focusing on the application of ML in clinical and pathological data integration, and dynamic treatment response prediction.
analysis.methods: The authors review how machine learning can be applied to analyze medical images, integrate clinical and pathological data, and predict treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy.
analysis.main_results: The authors highlight early but encouraging results from three areas: quantitative image analysis using ML, multimodal integration of clinical and pathological data, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that machine learning's greatest value lies in complementing existing tools, particularly for identifying patients unlikely to achieve fibrosis reversal with antiviral therapy alone, rather than replacing them.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that machine learning could enhance the precision of predicting treatment outcomes in chronic hepatitis B, aiding in personalized approaches to therapy and improving patient management.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The authors note that current models are based on small, single-center retrospective cohorts, which limits their generalizability and requires prospective multi-center validation for clinical adoption.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the potential of machine learning to improve the prediction of liver fibrosis reversal in chronic hepatitis B patients. It highlights the limitations of conventional clinical tools and emphasizes the need for more robust, personalized approaches. The authors suggest that ML can complement existing methods by identifying patients who may not benefit from antiviral therapy alone, but they caution that current models require validation in larger, multi-center studies to ensure their reliability and applicability in clinical settings.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of reliable methods for predicting individual treatment response to antiviral therapy in chronic hepatitis B patients, as long-term therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in some individuals but not all.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This opinion review discusses the potential of machine learning to improve prediction of fibrosis reversal in chronic hepatitis B, focusing on the application of ML in clinical and pathological data integration, and dynamic treatment response prediction.
analysis_en.methods: The authors review how machine learning can be applied to analyze medical images, integrate clinical and pathological data, and predict treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy.
analysis_en.main_results: The authors highlight early but encouraging results from three areas: quantitative image analysis using ML, multimodal integration of clinical and pathological data, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that machine learning's greatest value lies in complementing existing tools, particularly for identifying patients unlikely to achieve fibrosis reversal with antiviral therapy alone, rather than replacing them.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that machine learning could enhance the precision of predicting treatment outcomes in chronic hepatitis B, aiding in personalized approaches to therapy and improving patient management.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The authors note that current models are based on small, single-center retrospective cohorts, which limits their generalizability and requires prospective multi-center validation for clinical adoption.

papers.title_zh: 通过机器学习实现针对慢性乙型肝炎相关肝纤维化的个性化预测
papers.source_body_en: Although long-term antiviral therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in a considerable proportion of patients with chronic hepatitis B, treatment response differs markedly among individuals, and reliable methods for predicting who will benefit remain lacking. Conventional clinical tools such as liver stiffness measurement and the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index were originally dewsigned for cross-sectional staging rather than longitudinal prediction, and their ability to capture the dynamic process of fibrosis reversal is limited. In this opinion review, we discuss how machine learning (ML) may help address this unmet need. We focus on three areas where ML has shown early but encouraging results: Quantitative analysis of images using ML, integration of pathological and clinical data through multimodal models, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy. In our view, the greatest value of ML lies not in replacing existing assessment tools but in complementing them, particularly through the early identification of patients who are unlikely to achieve fibrosis reversal with antiviral therapy alone. However, we also caution that most current models have been developed from small, single-center retrospective cohorts, and their clinical adoption will require prospective multi-center validation, improved model interpretability, and adherence to standardized reporting frameworks.
papers.abstract_zh: 尽管长期抗病毒药物治疗可以逆转慢性乙型肝炎患者的肝纤维化,但个体对治疗的反应差异显著,目前仍缺乏可靠的预测方法。传统的临床工具如肝硬度测量和天门冬氨酸氨基转移酶与血小板比值指数最初设计用于横断面分期,而非纵向预测,其捕捉纤维化逆转动态过程的能力有限。在本观点综述中,我们讨论了机器学习(ML)如何帮助解决这一未满足的需求。我们重点关注了机器学习在三个方面的早期但有希望的结果:利用机器学习进行图像的定量分析、通过多模态模型整合病理和临床数据,以及基于抗病毒药物治疗期间的连续测量动态预测治疗反应。我们认为,机器学习的最大价值并不在于取代现有评估工具,而在于补充它们,特别是在早期识别那些仅通过抗病毒药物治疗难以实现纤维化逆转的患者方面。然而,我们也提醒,目前大多数模型都是基于小规模、单中心的回顾性队列研究开发的,其临床应用需要前瞻性多中心验证、提高模型的可解释性以及遵循标准化的报告框架。

papers.title: Point of Care Diagnostics for Hepatitis B and C in Low-resource Settings: A Narrative Review
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) and Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) continue to be major public health challenge especially in Low- and MiddleIncome Countries (LMICs), with poor laboratory capacity and the ability to detect the disease earlier and contribute to its management. Proper and timely diagnosis is crucial for clinical intervention and global elimination. The present narrative review explores the potential for the use of Point-Of-Care (POC) testing to enhance the testing of HBV and HCV in low-resource settings. Peer-reviewed literature, global health reports, and grey literature were reviewed to assess the state of the art of POC technologies, diagnostic performance, and implementation in resource-limited settings, as well as new developments. Existing challenges and future opportunities for improving access to timely and effective HBV and HCV diagnosis are also pointed out. New technologies and features, such as mobile healthcare integration, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered interpretation, and self-testing, enhance their capabilities. There are still areas of challenge, including uneven policy adoption, supply chain issues, and social stigma, that make it difficult to scale. POC diagnostics have the potential to accelerate hepatitis elimination by improving access to rapid testing. Their successful implementation requires strengthened health systems, trained healthcare workers, and integration into existing healthcare services.

source_records.abstract: Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) and Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) continue to be major public health challenge especially in Low- and MiddleIncome Countries (LMICs), with poor laboratory capacity and the ability to detect the disease earlier and contribute to its management. Proper and timely diagnosis is crucial for clinical intervention and global elimination. The present narrative review explores the potential for the use of Point-Of-Care (POC) testing to enhance the testing of HBV and HCV in low-resource settings. Peer-reviewed literature, global health reports, and grey literature were reviewed to assess the state of the art of POC technologies, diagnostic performance, and implementation in resource-limited settings, as well as new developments. Existing challenges and future opportunities for improving access to timely and effective HBV and HCV diagnosis are also pointed out. New technologies and features, such as mobile healthcare integration, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered interpretation, and self-testing, enhance their capabilities. There are still areas of challenge, including uneven policy adoption, supply chain issues, and social stigma, that make it difficult to scale. POC diagnostics have the potential to accelerate hepatitis elimination by improving access to rapid testing. Their successful implementation requires strengthened health systems, trained healthcare workers, and integration into existing healthcare services.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review evaluates the potential of Point-Of-Care (POC) diagnostics to improve the detection and management of Hepatitis B virus (HBV) in low-resource settings. It highlights the importance of timely diagnosis for clinical intervention and global elimination, noting that POC technologies can enhance accessibility and effectiveness. The review identifies key challenges, including uneven policy adoption, supply chain issues, and social stigma, which hinder the scalability of POC diagnostics. It also discusses the integration of new technologies, such as mobile healthcare and AI-powered interpretation, to strengthen diagnostic capabilities. The review underscores the need for improved health systems, trained personnel, and policy support to fully realize the benefits of POC testing for HBV.

papers.abstract_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 和丙型肝炎病毒 (HCV) 仍然是主要的公共卫生挑战,特别是在低收入和中等收入国家 (LMIC),实验室能力较差,早期发现疾病并有助于其管理的能力较差。正确、及时的诊断对于临床干预和全球消除至关重要。本叙述性综述探讨了使用即时护理 (POC) 检测来加强资源匮乏环境中 HBV 和 HCV 检测的潜力。审查了同行评审的文献、全球健康报告和灰色文献,以评估 POC 技术的最新技术、诊断性能、资源有限环境中的实施以及新的发展。还指出了改善及时有效的 HBV 和 HCV 诊断 的可及性的现有挑战和未来机遇。移动医疗集成、人工智能 (AI) 支持的解释和自我测试等新技术和功能增强了他们的能力。仍然存在一些挑战,包括政策采用不平衡、供应链问题和社会耻辱,导致难以扩展。POC 诊断有可能通过改善快速检测的机会来加速消除肝炎。它们的成功实施需要加强卫生系统、训练有素的医疗保健人员以及融入现有的医疗保健服务。

papers.title: Development of an investigational epigenetic silencer therapy to transcriptionally inactivate viral DNA in chronic hepatitis B.
papers.abstract: Approved chronic hepatitis B therapies rarely result in functional cure, as they fail to permanently silence all transcriptionally active hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA. CRMA-1001 employs an optimized epigenetic silencer that represses viral transcription through targeted deposition of DNA methylation on episomal and integrated HBV DNAs. Here we showed that in HBV mouse models, a single dose of CRMA-1001 produced >3-log10 reductions in viral biomarkers, which correlated with de novo methylation of HBV DNA. Three doses resulted in up to 90% of animals with undetectable hepatitis B surface antigen and HBV DNA by 6 months post treatment. In non-human primates, CRMA-1001 induced transient liver transaminase elevations only at the highest dose tested. Expression and DNA methylation profiling revealed no detectable unintended targets in the human genome. These findings support the initiation of clinical development of CRMA-1001 as a finite treatment course with the potential for functional cure in individuals living with chronic hepatitis B. A nanomedicine comprising a guide RNA and an mRNA co-encapsulated in a lipid nanoparticle for delivery to hepatocytes holds promise for a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B through epigenetic silencing.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to address the limitations of current hepatitis B virus (HBV) therapies, which rarely achieve a functional cure by failing to silence all transcriptionally active HBV DNA. The research focused on CRMA-1001, an epigenetic silencer designed to repress viral transcription through DNA methylation. In HBV mouse models, a single dose of CRMA-1001 led to >3-log10 reductions in viral biomarkers, with three doses achieving up to 90% undetectable hepatitis B surface antigen and HBV DNA by 6 months post-treatment. In non-human primates, the therapy caused transient liver transaminase elevations only at the highest dose tested, and no unintended targets were detected in the human genome. These results suggest that CRMA-1001 could be a promising finite treatment for chronic HBV, potentially leading to a functional cure. However, the study's findings are based on animal models, and further clinical trials are needed to confirm efficacy and safety in humans.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 批准的慢性乙型肝炎疗法很少能实现功能性治愈,因为它们无法永久沉默所有转录活跃的乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)DNA。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: CRMA-1001采用了一种优化的表观遗传沉默剂,通过在环状和整合的HBV DNA上靶向沉积DNA甲基化来抑制病毒转录。
analysis_zh.main_results: 三次剂量后,6个月治疗后,高达90%的动物检测不到乙型肝炎表面抗原和HBV DNA。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在非人灵长类动物中,CRMA-1001仅在最高剂量测试时诱导了短暂的肝转氨酶升高。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 表达和DNA甲基化分析显示,在人类基因组中未检测到可识别的意外靶点。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 这些发现支持启动CRMA-1001的临床开发,作为一种有限的治疗疗程,可能在与慢性乙型肝炎共存的个体中实现功能性治愈。

media_mentions.title: Development of an investigational epigenetic silencer therapy to transcriptionally inactivate viral DNA in chronic hepatitis B - Nature
media_mentions.rss_summary_html: Development of an investigational epigenetic silencer therapy to transcriptionally inactivate viral DNA in chronic hepatitis B  Nature
media_mentions.excerpt_original: Development of an investigational epigenetic silencer therapy to transcriptionally inactivate viral DNA in chronic hepatitis B Nature
media_mentions.priority_tier_reason: 新闻聚合或正文证据有限，作为补充信息
media_mentions.content_title: Development of an investigational epigenetic silencer therapy to transcriptionally inactivate viral DNA in chronic hepatitis B - Nature Biomedical Engineering
media_mentions.content: Ethics statement All studies involving the use of animals were conducted in compliance with animal care and use protocols approved by institutional animal care and use committees (IACUC) of corresponding testing facilities: Wuxi Apptec, nChroma Bio and AltaSciences. The health assessment of animals was performed in accordance with IACUC standard operating procedures and guidelines of each testing facility. In silico HBV conservation and gRNA designs Guide target conservation analysis was performed by assessing exact matches between the target sequence including presence of the dSpCas9 NGG PAM and the reference genomes with A–E genotypes found in HBVdb21 using NCBI BLAST40. The percentage of exact matches per genotype was used to assess conservation. RNA production Using standard methods by commercial suppliers, 100-mer gRNAs were chemically synthesized. The gRNAs used for in vitro screens contain 2′-O-methylation and phosphorothioate linkages at the three terminal nucleotides of both the 5′ and 3′ ends, as previously described15. Subsequent studies in vitro and in vivo employed gRNAs containing both end-modifications as well as a proprietary pattern of 2′-O-methylation throughout the sequence. All gRNA target sequence used in this study are presented in Supplementary Table 1. mRNA was produced via in vitro transcription and purification. Plasmids containing an epigenetic silencer or a control construct were linearized by restriction digest and used as a template with T7 RNA polymerase, NTPs (including N1-methylpseudouridine) and cap analogue. mRNAs either underwent enzymatic A-tailing or contained an encoded polyA in the template, as previously described15. The amino acid sequences of all constructs used in these studies are presented in Supplementary Table 2. LNP formulations Small-scale LNP formulations of epigenetic silencer mRNA and gRNA for screens and initial HepG2.2.15 studies were prepared using GenVoy-ILM kits. Formulations were optimized with an aim to attain LNPs of uniform size and high encapsulation efficiency. The ratio of lipids to the total RNA cargo, comprising mRNA and gRNA, was calculated on the basis of the molar weights of lipids and RNAs. Medium-scale LNP formulations used in in vitro, rodent and NHP studies contained an ionizable cationic lipid proprietary to Acuitas Therapeutics, as well as phosphatidylcholine/cholesterol/PEG-lipid. The proprietary lipid and LNP compositions are described in patent application WO2020146805A1. The RNAs were mixed and encapsulated in LNP using a self-assembly process as described previously15,41. The resulting LNPs had a diameter ≤70 nm as measured by dynamic light scattering using a Zetasizer Nano ZS (Malvern Instruments) instrument and encapsulation efficiencies of more than 97% as measured by Quant-iT RiboGreen Assay (Life Technologies). In vitro studies HepG2.2.15 and PLC/PRF/5 cell culture and treatment HepG2.2.15 cells were cultured in DMEM (Gibco, 11965092) with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) (Gibco, A5670501) and 1% penicillin–streptomycin (Gibco, 15140122). A day before treatment, 20,000 cells per well were seeded in collagen type I-coated 96-well plates. On the following day, the cells were treated with 100 μl of fresh medium supplemented with LNP-formulated epigenetic silencers at a single dose of 0.5 μg ml−1 or an 8-point serial dilution (4–0.031 μg ml−1) and/or 1 μg ml−1 of recombinant human apolipoprotein E3 (rhApoE3) (a supplement to facilitate LNP transfection in cell culture), also referred to as mock treatment. Plates were maintained and subcultured (cell trypsinization every 3–4 days), and supernatants or cell samples were collected at various time points from 6 h to 27 days after treatment and stored at −80 °C until analysis. Studies to evaluate EE protein were performed in 24-well plate format, and 118,750 cells per well were seeded and treatment with 500 μl of fresh medium supplemented with 1 μg ml−1 of rhApoE3 and or 1 μg ml−1 of CRMA-1001. PLC/PRF/5 cells (ATCC, CRL-8024) were cultured in Eagle’s minimum essential medium (Corning, 10-009-CV) with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin–streptomycin and maintained as described above for 96-well plates. Cells were treated with 1 μg ml−1 of rhApoE3 (mock-treatment control) and/or 1 μg ml−1 of CRMA-1001, then supernatants were collected at 7 and 14 days after treatment and stored at −80 °C until analysis. PHH cell culture, infection and treatment PHHs isolated from humanized mouse liver (PXB-cells) (PhoenixBio)42 were received pre-plated in 24-well plates and maintained in culture medium (dHCGM medium (PhoenixBio) and 10% FBS) and incubated at 37 °C and 5% CO 2 . To establish HBV infection, 4 days before treatment, HBV was diluted in infection medium (dHCGM, 10% FBS, 4% PEG8000 and and 2.5% DMSO) at a multiplicity of genome equivalents (MGE) of 2,000 per cell of HBV genotype D (Imquest BioSciences). The supernatant was collected from all wells and replaced with infection medium. The following day, 16 h after infection, the medium was removed, cells were washed twice with Dulbecco’s phosphate-buffered saline (DPBS) and 500 μl of fresh maintenance medium (dHCGM, 10% FBS and 2.5% DMSO) was added to each well. For studies with uninfected PHHs, cells were maintained in culture medium upon treatment. On the day of treatment (day 0), PHHs were treated with 500 μl culture medium supplemented with 1 μg ml−1 of rhApoE3 and 0.5 or 1 μg ml−1 CRMA-1001 or rhApoE3 only (mock-treatment control). At 14 days post treatment, the supernatants were collected, cells washed and both stored at −80 °C until analysis. Primary HSECs and primary HAdCC treatment Primary HSECs (Innoprot and Accegen) from three different human donors were cultured in medium (endothelial cell medium (ScienCell) with 5% FBS, 1% penicillin–streptomycin and 1% endothelial cell growth supplement (ScienCell)) and incubated at 37 °C and 5% CO 2 . A day before test or control article treatment, 10,000 cells per well were seeded into a 96-well tissue culture plate precoated with 150 μg ml−1 of human fibronectin and containing 200 μl culture medium. On the day of treatment (day 0), culture medium was replaced with 100 μl of fresh medium containing 1 μg ml−1 of rhApoE3 and CRMA-1001 or control articles. On day 14, the cells were washed with 200 μl DPBS per well, lysed with 63 μl Beckman Coulter Buffer LBE with Proteinase K, incubated for 30 min at room temperature and frozen at −80 °C in plate format. Primary HAdCCs (Accegen) were cultured in medium (Mesenchymal Stem Cell Medium (Innoprot) with 5% FBS, 1% penicillin–streptomycin and 1% Mesenchymal Stem Cell Growth Serum (Innoprot)) and incubated at 37 °C and 5% CO 2 . A day before test or control article treatment, 10,000 cells per well were seeded into a 96-well tissue culture plate precoated with 150 μg ml−1 of poly-l-lysine (Sigma-Aldrich) and containing 200 μl culture medium. On the day of treatment (day 0), the culture medium was replaced with 100 μl of medium containing 1 μg ml−1 of rhApoE3 and CRMA-1001 or control articles. The plates were maintained and cells subcultured (cell trypsinization every 3–4 days, followed by transfer of ~10,000 cells to a new 96-well culture plate with fresh medium). On day 14, cells were washed with 200 μl DPBS per well, lysed with 63 μl Beckman Coulter Buffer LBE with Proteinase K, incubated for 30 min at room temperature and frozen at −80 °C in plate format. Cell viability assays Viability was assessed using Cell Titer-Glo (Promega, G924B) or Cell Titer-Blue Assays (Promega, G8080) according to the manufacturer’s recommendations. The fluorescent signal obtained was measured using the Infinite 200 PRO Microplate Reader with a 560Ex/590Em filter set (TECAN). To account for technical variability in cell number during subculture, the secreted antigen concentrations were normalized to cell viability in each individual well and expressed as a percentage relative to control-treated cells. Primary screening in vitro in HepG2-NTCP cells For the initial screening experiments, EEs were delivered to HepG2-NTCP cells as three individual mRNAs, each encoding an engineered transcriptional repressor as previously described43 (dCas9-KRAB mRNA, DNMT3A mRNA and DNMT3L mRNA) as well as the candidate single guide RNA mixed at a 1:1:1:4 ratio. The RNA mix was formulated into LNPs using the Genvoy-ILM Lipid Mix kit (Precision Nanosystems). The HepG2-NTCP cell line was generated using HepG2 cells acquired from ATCC and transduced with a lentiviral vector to stably express the NTCP receptor. Cells were maintained in DMEM (Gibco, 21969035) supplemented with 10% FBS, 1% of glutamine and 1% penicillin–streptomycin. HepG2-NTCP cells were plated at 20,000 cells per well in collagen-coated 96-well plates and infected 24 h later with HBV genotype D at 5,000 MGE using DMEM medium supplemented with 4% PEG8000 and 2.5% DMSO. At 16 h post infection, the medium was removed, and the cells were washed with PBS and maintained in DMEM medium supplemented with 2.5% DMSO. Subsequently, 4 days after infection, the cells were treated with LNPs, and the medium was changed 1 and 3 days after LNP treatment. Finally, the supernatant was collected 6 days after transfection, and HBeAg and HBsAg levels were quantified by ELISA (Dia.Pro) and cell viability by Cell Titer-Blue Assay. HBV infection and the antiviral effect of treatments was analysed by HBeAg/HBsAg quantification. Guide potency was assessed by normalizing HBsAg and HBeAg measurement for each guide by the cell viability value for that guide. In vivo studies Tg-HBV mice The study was conducted at WuXi AppTec in accordance with IACUC guidelines. C57BL/6-HBV transgenic mice (Tg-HBV), 5–6 weeks old, carrying two copies per diploid host genome of the 1.28× genotype A HBV genome24 were obtained from Beijing Vitalstar Biotechnology. All animals were acclimated for 10 days during which the baseline levels of circulating HBV biomarkers (HBsAg, HBV DNA, and HBeAg) were measured. On day 0, all animals received a single i.v. bolus administration of vehicle, HBV-EE4000 (0.5, 1 and 3 mg kg−1) or CRMA-1001 (0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 mg kg−1). Male C57BL/6J mice (6–8 weeks old) were obtained from The Jackson Laboratory. Following acclimation, mice were transduced with AAV8-HBV1.2 (genotype D; Signagen, SL100862) via i.v. injection at a dose of 3 × 1011 viral genomes. Circulating HBsAg levels were assessed at 2, 3 and 4 weeks post transduction to establish baseline levels and determine eligibility for study enrollment. Mice with mean baseline HBsAg levels between 5,000 IU ml−1 and 50,000 IU ml−1 were included. Animals meeting this criterion were randomized into treatment groups, with the goal of achieving an average baseline HBsAg level of approximately 10,000 IU ml−1 per group. Groups received a single i.v. infusion over 1 h of vehicle (n = 3) (0.9% sodium chloride) or CRMA-1001 at 2 mg kg−1 (n = 16). Animals were euthanized at 1 h, 24 h, 7 days and 28 days post infusion to assess PKs and biodistribution of CRMA-1001. The Good Laboratory Practice toxicity study consisted of male and female naive monkeys randomized into four groups of three to five animals per sex per group. Groups received three i.v. infusions for 1 h of vehicle (n = 8) (0.9% sodium chloride), or CRMA-1001 at dose levels of 0.5 mg kg−1 (n = 6), 1 mg kg−1 (n = 10) or 2 mg kg−1 (n = 10), every 4 weeks. Animals were fasted for at least 4 h before serum chemistry collections with access to water. Blood was collected from a peripheral vein, and serum was obtained for clinical chemistry analyses using a clinical analyzer. Serum chemistry, including ALT, AST and TBIL, was monitored at baseline and through the duration of the study, up to 4 weeks following the last CRMA-1001 dose administration. Assessments of the biodistribution of CRMA-1001 included measurements of the effector mRNA in tissues. In brief, for the effector mRNA analyses, RNA was extracted from monkey plasma using QIAGEN QIAcube HT kits, and a reverse transcription (RT)–ddPCR assay was performed using the following primers: effector mRNA primer 1 (CTGGGACCCTAAGAAGTACG), primer 2 (GCAGCTCTTTCACACTCTTC) and probe (ACAGCCCCACCGTGGCCTAT). The mobile phase was nebulized using heated nitrogen set to TurboSpray positive ionization mode and the compounds were detected using tandem mass spectrometry. For biodistribution studies, tissue RNA was extracted using QIAGEN QIAcube HT kits, and an RT–ddPCR assay for the effector mRNA was performed using the primers described above. papers.title: Molecular Evolution of Hepatitis B Virus in India: Insights into Genotype Diversity and Recombination
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a major public health problem in India, with considerable genetic variability arising out of evolutionary selection pressure, recombination events and reverse-transcription stage in its life cycle. This affects the transmission patterns, disease chronicity, and treatment response of the virus. Although HBV genotypes A, C, and D have been described in India, detailed whole-genome sequence data are scarce. Methods Residual HBsAg positive samples (n = 1963), received for inter-laboratory quality control or for referral diagnostic testing between 2006 and 2023 were screened, and n = 172 of these were positive for HBV DNA by realtime PCR. HBV DNA positive samples with high viral load (n = 32), collected from nine states of India, were used for whole-genome sequencing. DNA extracted these serum samples was subjected to whole-genome sequencing (WGS) on the Oxford Nanopore Technology (ONT) MinION platform. Genotype-specific tiled amplicons (~ 1000 bp) were used for library preparation. Consensus genomes were assembled, genotyped, and phylogenetically analysed using MEGA v11.0. Recombinant sequences were characterized further by SimPlot v3.5.1 boot scanning and confirmed with χ2 testing of phylogenetically informative sites. Results HBV genotype D (70.96%) was found to be common genotype in several Indian states, with genotype A (3.22%) present in central and southern states and genotype C (6.45%) in the northeast. Notably, five samples showed evidence of recombination events, including genotypes A, C, and D. There were two recombinants in West Bengal, and one each in Chhattisgarh, Assam, and Maharashtra. SimPlot analysis of representative isolates showed clearly demarcated recombination breakpoints. Phylogenetic reconstruction also attested to the mosaic character of these genomes. Conclusions The present study emphasizes the genetic heterogeneity and evolutionary dynamics of HBV in India, and recombination as a key mechanism adding to viral diversity. The success in utilizing ONT for WGS of HBV directly from serum samples illustrates its utility for scalable genomic surveillance. The initiation of a nationwide HBV sequencing program will be pivotal in tracking emerging variants, informing therapeutic interventions, and facilitating India's role in the global HBV elimination drive.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the molecular evolution of Hepatitis B virus (HBV) in India, focusing on genotype diversity and recombination. The research highlights the genetic variability of HBV due to evolutionary pressures and recombination events, which influence transmission patterns, disease chronicity, and treatment response. Whole-genome sequencing of 32 HBV DNA positive samples from nine Indian states revealed genotype D as the most prevalent, followed by A and C. Five samples showed evidence of recombination, with clearly demarcated breakpoints identified through SimPlot analysis. The study underscores the importance of genomic surveillance in tracking HBV variants and informing public health strategies. The use of Oxford Nanopore Technology for direct sequencing from serum samples demonstrates its potential for scalable monitoring. The findings emphasize the need for a nationwide HBV sequencing program to support global elimination efforts.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)是印度的主要公共卫生问题,其显著的遗传变异源于进化选择压力、重组事件以及其生命周期中的逆转录阶段。这影响了病毒的基因组模式、慢性化程度以及免疫应答。尽管在印度已描述了HBV基因型A、C和D,但详细的全基因组序列数据仍然稀缺。方法 从2006年至2023年间接收用于实验室间质量控制或转诊诊断测试的HBsAg阳性残留样本(n = 1963)中筛选,其中n = 172份样本通过实时PCR检测出HBV DNA阳性。从印度九个州收集的HBV DNA阳性样本中,病毒载量高的n = 32份样本用于全基因组测序。从这些血清样本中提取的DNA在Oxford Nanopore Technology(ONT)MinION平台上进行全基因组测序(WGS)。使用基因型特异性拼接扩增子(约1000 bp)进行文库制备。使用MEGA v11.0软件组装、基因型鉴定并进行系统发育分析。进一步通过SimPlot v3.5.1的boot扫描分析重组序列,并通过系统发育信息位点的χ2检验进行确认。结果 在多个印度州中,HBV基因型D(70.96%)是最常见的基因型,基因型A(3.22%)存在于中部和南部州,基因型C(6.45%)则分布在东北部。值得注意的是,有五份样本显示出重组事件的证据,包括基因型A、C和D。在西孟加拉邦发现了两份重组样本,在恰特泰斯加尔邦、阿萨姆邦和马哈拉施特拉邦各发现一份。对代表性分离株的SimPlot分析清楚地显示了重组断点。系统发育重建也证实了这些基因组的镶嵌特性。结论 本研究强调了印度HBV的遗传异质性和进化动态,并指出重组是增加病毒多样性的关键机制。利用ONT平台直接从血清样本中进行HBV全基因组测序的成功经验,展示了其在可扩展基因组监测中的应用价值。启动全国范围的HBV测序计划对于追踪新兴变异株、指导治疗干预以及促进印度在全球HBV消除行动中的作用至关重要。

papers.title: Determinants of Adult Hepatitis B Vaccine Uptake in a High-Endemic Setting
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Adult hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccination remains a critical yet underutilized component of viral hepatitis prevention in many high-endemic settings. Although infant HBV vaccination has been widely integrated into national immunization programmes, adult vaccination often depends on individual awareness, healthcare access, and provider recommendation. Community-based evidence on the determinants of adult HBV vaccine uptake is needed to inform adult immunization strategies in resource-constrained settings. Objective To examine the individual- and health-system level factors associated with adult HBV vaccine uptake in a community-based population in a high-endemic setting and identify priorities for strengthening adult vaccination programmes. Methods We conducted a community-based cross-sectional survey among adults in Minna, Nigeria, using multistage sampling. Data on sociodemographic characteristics, HBV-related knowledge, healthcare access, and vaccination status were collected using interviewer-administered questionnaires. Modified Poisson regression with robust variance estimation was used to identify factors independently associated with vaccine uptake, with adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) reported. Results Among 426 participants, 167 (39.2%) had received at least one dose of HBV vaccine, and 38.5% had completed the vaccination series. Community-based evidence on the determinants of adult HBV vaccine uptake is needed to inform adult immunization strategies in resource-constrained settings. Objective To examine the individual- and health-system level factors associated with adult HBV vaccine uptake in a community-based population in a high-endemic setting and identify priorities for strengthening adult vaccination programmes. Although infant HBV vaccination has been widely integrated into national immunization programmes, adult vaccination often depends on individual awareness, healthcare access, and provider recommendation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a community-based cross-sectional survey among adults in Minna, Nigeria, using multistage sampling. analysis.methods: Data on sociodemographic characteristics, HBV-related knowledge, healthcare access, and vaccination status were collected using interviewer-administered questionnaires. analysis.main_results: Among 426 participants, 167 (39.2%) had received at least one dose of HBV vaccine, and 38.5% had completed the vaccination series. In bivariate analyses, vaccine uptake was significantly associated with education, occupation, residence type, ward, religion, HBV knowledge, and health worker recommendation (all p.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights the importance of sociodemographic and health-system factors in influencing adult HBV vaccine uptake, providing actionable insights for improving immunization strategies in high-endemic regions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform targeted interventions to improve adult HBV vaccination rates, particularly in resource-constrained settings where health worker recommendations and awareness play a pivotal role in vaccine uptake.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which cannot establish causality, and by potential biases related to self-reported data. analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the determinants of adult hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccine uptake in a high-endemic setting in Minna, Nigeria. It highlights the underutilization of adult HBV vaccination despite its importance in viral hepatitis prevention. The research focuses on individual and health-system level factors, such as education, occupation, healthcare access, and provider recommendations, which were found to significantly influence vaccine uptake. The study employs a community-based cross-sectional survey with multistage sampling and uses modified Poisson regression to analyze associations. Among 426 participants, 39.2% had received at least one dose of HBV vaccine, and 38.5% had completed the series. The findings suggest that improving health worker recommendations and increasing awareness could enhance adult vaccination rates. However, the study's cross-sectional design limits its ability to establish causality, and the evidence is moderate in strength due to potential biases and the reliance on self-reported data.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 在许多高流行地区,成人乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)疫苗接种仍然是病毒性肝炎预防中关键但未被充分利用的组成部分。尽管婴儿HBV疫苗接种已被广泛纳入国家免疫计划,但成人疫苗接种往往依赖于个人意识、医疗保健可及性和医疗提供者的推荐。需要基于社区的证据来了解成人HBV疫苗接种的影响因素,以指导资源匮乏地区的成人疫苗接种策略。目的 在高流行地区的社区人群中,探讨与成人HBV疫苗接种率相关的个体及卫生系统层面的因素,并确定加强成人疫苗接种计划的优先事项。方法 我们在尼日利亚Minna市对成人进行了基于社区的横断面调查,采用多阶段抽样方法。通过访谈员填写的问卷收集了有关社会人口学特征、HBV相关知识、医疗保健可及性以及疫苗接种状态的数据。使用带有稳健方差估计的修改泊松回归分析来确定与疫苗接种独立相关的因素,并报告了调整后的比值比(aPRs)和95%置信区间(CIs)。结果 在426名参与者中,167人(39.2%)至少接种过一剂HBV疫苗,38.5%的人完成了疫苗接种系列。在双变量分析中,疫苗接种与教育程度、职业、居住类型、选区、宗教信仰、HBV知识和医疗工作者推荐显著相关(所有p值均<0.05)。解释与创新性 本研究强调了社会人口学和卫生系统因素在影响成人HBV疫苗接种中的重要性,为改善高流行地区的疫苗接种策略提供了可操作的见解。科学与公共卫生意义 这些发现可以用于制定有针对性的干预措施,以提高成人HBV疫苗接种率,特别是在资源匮乏地区,医疗工作者的推荐和个人意识在疫苗接种中起着关键作用。局限性与证据强度 本研究的局限性在于其横断面设计,无法确定因果关系,且可能存在与自我报告数据相关的偏倚。由于研究的观察性质和缺乏纵向随访,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Intradermal hepatitis B vaccination with or without Imiquimod in cirrhosis after prior vaccine nonresponse: A Randomised Trial.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Patients with cirrhosis show impaired immune responses to standard intramuscular (IM) hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccination, resulting in low seroconversion rates. Intradermal (ID) vaccination and topical imiquimod have been proposed as strategies to enhance vaccine immunogenicity. We conducted a randomized controlled pilot trial to compare three HBV revaccination strategies in patients with advanced chronic liver disease (ACLD) who previously failed standard IM vaccination: IM revaccination, ID revaccination, and ID revaccination combined with imiquimod (ID+IMQ). The primary endpoint was seroconversion at Month 7, defined as anti-HBs titres ≥10 mIU/mL. METHODS: This monocentric, prospective study included 59 patients with ACLD and anti-HBs titres <10 mIU/mL after prior HBV vaccination. Patients were randomized (1:1:1) to receive either IM vaccination (n=19; Engerix-B® 20 μg IM at Months 0, 1 and 6), ID vaccination (n=19; two 10 μg ID injections at the same time points), or ID vaccination preceded by topical imiquimod 5% application (n=21). RESULTS: In the intention-to-treat analysis, seroprotection rates at month 7 were 36.8% in the IM group, 84.2% in the ID group, and 66.7% in the ID+IMQ group (p<0.01). After Bonferroni correction, only the ID versus IM comparison remained statistically significant (p=0.003). Geometric mean anti-HBs titres were significantly higher in the ID (116 mIU/mL) and ID+IMQ (107 mIU/mL) groups compared with the IM group (12 mIU/mL) (p=0.004). No severe vaccine-related adverse reactions were observed. CONCLUSIONS: Intradermal HBV revaccination significantly improves seroconversion in non-responder patients with ACLD compared with IM vaccination, without additional benefit from imiquimod. These results support further evaluation of intradermal vaccination without imiquimod in a phase 3 trial. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: The study protocol has been registered before the patients' recruitment, in the European Clinical Trials Database (EudraCT) of the European Medicine Agency (2021-000644-22), as well as on ClinicalTrials.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of intradermal (ID) hepatitis B vaccination, with or without imiquimod, in patients with cirrhosis who previously failed standard intramuscular (IM) vaccination. A randomized controlled pilot trial was conducted with 59 patients with advanced chronic liver disease (ACLD) and anti-HBs titres <10 mIU/mL. The results showed that seroprotection rates were significantly higher in the ID group (84.2%) compared to the IM group (36.8%), with no additional benefit from imiquimod. papers.title_zh: 肝硬化患者在先前标准肌内接种乙型肝炎疫苗失败后,采用皮内接种乙型肝炎疫苗(含或不含咪喹莫特):一项随机试验。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Patients with cirrhosis show impaired immune responses to standard intramuscular (IM) hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccination, resulting in low seroconversion rates. Intradermal (ID) vaccination and topical imiquimod have been proposed as strategies to enhance vaccine immunogenicity. We conducted a randomized controlled pilot trial to compare three HBV revaccination strategies in patients with advanced chronic liver disease (ACLD) who previously failed standard IM vaccination: IM revaccination, ID revaccination, and ID revaccination combined with imiquimod (ID+IMQ). The primary endpoint was seroconversion at Month 7, defined as anti-HBs titres ≥10 mIU/mL. METHODS: This monocentric, prospective study included 59 patients with ACLD and anti-HBs titres <10 mIU/mL after prior HBV vaccination. Patients were randomized (1:1:1) to receive either IM vaccination (n=19; Engerix-B® 20 μg IM at Months 0, 1 and 6), ID vaccination (n=19; two 10 μg ID injections at the same time points), or ID vaccination preceded by topical imiquimod 5% application (n=21). RESULTS: In the intention-to-treat analysis, seroprotection rates at month 7 were 36.8% in the IM group, 84.2% in the ID group, and 66.7% in the ID+IMQ group (p<0.01). After Bonferroni correction, only the ID versus IM comparison remained statistically significant (p=0.003). Geometric mean anti-HBs titres were significantly higher in the ID (116 mIU/mL) and ID+IMQ (107 mIU/mL) groups compared with the IM group (12 mIU/mL) (p=0.004). No severe vaccine-related adverse reactions were observed. CONCLUSIONS: Intradermal HBV revaccination significantly improves seroconversion in non-responder patients with ACLD compared with IM vaccination, without additional benefit from imiquimod. These results support further evaluation of intradermal vaccination without imiquimod in a phase 3 trial. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: The study protocol has been registered before the patients' recruitment, in the European Clinical Trials Database (EudraCT) of the European Medicine Agency (2021-000644-22), as well as on ClinicalTrials.

papers.title: Effectiveness of Radio Messages in Reducing Public Hesitancy Toward Hepatitis B Vaccination in Selected North-Central States of Nigeria
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B remains a major public health challenge in Nigeria, with low vaccination uptake exacerbated by widespread public hesitancy fueled by misinformation, cultural misconceptions, and limited access to reliable health information, particularly in the North-Central states. Addressing this challenge necessitates effective health communication strategies capable of improving awareness, trust, and vaccine acceptance. This study examined the effectiveness of radio messages in reducing public hesitancy toward Hepatitis B vaccination, guided by the Theory of Planned Behavior, which was adopted due to its emphasis on understanding how attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control influence intention and health-related decision-making. Employing a survey research design, data were collected through structured questionnaires administered to residents in selected states, complemented by secondary data obtained from radio program archives and public health reports. Questionnaire responses were analyzed using simple percentages to quantify trends in perception, knowledge, and behavior, while secondary data underwent qualitative content analysis to assess message framing, cultural relevance, and persuasive strategies. Findings revealed that the effectiveness of radio messages was significantly undermined by ineffective message design, cultural misalignment, and weak persuasive content, limiting knowledge acquisition, trust building, and fear reduction, thereby sustaining vaccine hesitancy. Additionally, radio’s potential as a health communication tool was constrained by infrastructural limitations, diverse audience characteristics, linguistic barriers, inadequate programming strategies, and insufficient community engagement, all of which diminished message reach, relevance, and influence on vaccination decisions. The study recommends that radio messages be carefully evaluated and redesigned to ensure cultural relevance, clarity, and persuasive content that builds trust and reduces fear, and that radio stations and health authorities address infrastructural and audience-related challenges by expanding coverage to remote areas, incorporating multiple local languages, and adopting engaging programming strategies such as interactive talk shows and testimonials to enhance public receptivity and uptake of Hepatitis B vaccination.

source_records.title: Effectiveness of Radio Messages in Reducing Public Hesitancy Toward Hepatitis B Vaccination in Selected North-Central States of Nigeria
source_records.abstract: Hepatitis B remains a major public health challenge in Nigeria, with low vaccination uptake exacerbated by widespread public hesitancy fueled by misinformation, cultural misconceptions, and limited access to reliable health information, particularly in the North-Central states. Addressing this challenge necessitates effective health communication strategies capable of improving awareness, trust, and vaccine acceptance. This study examined the effectiveness of radio messages in reducing public hesitancy toward Hepatitis B vaccination, guided by the Theory of Planned Behavior, which was adopted due to its emphasis on understanding how attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control influence intention and health-related decision-making. Employing a survey research design, data were collected through structured questionnaires administered to residents in selected states, complemented by secondary data obtained from radio program archives and public health reports. Questionnaire responses were analyzed using simple percentages to quantify trends in perception, knowledge, and behavior, while secondary data underwent qualitative content analysis to assess message framing, cultural relevance, and persuasive strategies. Findings revealed that the effectiveness of radio messages was significantly undermined by ineffective message design, cultural misalignment, and weak persuasive content, limiting knowledge acquisition, trust building, and fear reduction, thereby sustaining vaccine hesitancy. Additionally, radio’s potential as a health communication tool was constrained by infrastructural limitations, diverse audience characteristics, linguistic barriers, inadequate programming strategies, and insufficient community engagement, all of which diminished message reach, relevance, and influence on vaccination decisions. The study recommends that radio messages be carefully evaluated and redesigned to ensure cultural relevance, clarity, and persuasive content that builds trust and reduces fear, and that radio stations and health authorities address infrastructural and audience-related challenges by expanding coverage to remote areas, incorporating multiple local languages, and adopting engaging programming strategies such as interactive talk shows and testimonials to enhance public receptivity and uptake of Hepatitis B vaccination.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study focuses on the effectiveness of radio messages in reducing public hesitancy toward Hepatitis B vaccination in selected North-Central states of Nigeria. The central question is whether radio messages can improve awareness, trust, and vaccine acceptance among the population, particularly in the context of misinformation, cultural misconceptions, and limited access to reliable health information.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review employs a survey research design, collecting data through structured questionnaires administered to residents in selected states. Secondary data were obtained from radio program archives and public health reports. Questionnaire responses were analyzed using simple percentages to quantify trends in perception, knowledge, and behavior, while secondary data underwent qualitative content analysis to assess message framing, cultural relevance, and persuasive strategies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study found that radio messages were ineffective in reducing public hesitancy toward Hepatitis B vaccination due to poor message design, cultural misalignment, and weak persuasive content. These factors limited knowledge acquisition, trust building, and fear reduction, thereby sustaining vaccine hesitancy. The findings suggest that radio as a health communication tool has significant limitations in the context of Hepatitis B vaccination in the North-Central states of Nigeria.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study highlights the limitations of radio messages in addressing public hesitancy, but it does not provide comparative data with other communication strategies. There is no mention of how the effectiveness of radio messages might vary across different demographic groups or how other factors such as socioeconomic status or education level might influence vaccine acceptance. The evidence also lacks information on the long-term impact of radio messages on vaccination behavior.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The study recommends that radio messages be carefully evaluated and redesigned to ensure cultural relevance, clarity, and persuasive content that builds trust and reduces fear. It also suggests that radio stations and health authorities should address infrastructural and audience-related challenges by expanding coverage to remote areas, incorporating multiple local languages, and adopting engaging programming strategies such as interactive talk shows and testimonials to enhance public receptivity and uptake of Hepatitis B vaccination.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the effectiveness of radio messages in reducing public hesitancy toward Hepatitis B vaccination in selected North-Central states of Nigeria. The study found that radio messages were ineffective due to poor design, cultural misalignment, and weak persuasive content, which limited knowledge acquisition and trust building. The review highlights the need for careful evaluation and redesign of radio messages to ensure cultural relevance and clarity, as well as addressing infrastructural and audience-related challenges to improve vaccine uptake. The findings suggest that radio, while a potential health communication tool, requires strategic improvements to be effective in this context.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本研究聚焦于在尼日利亚北中部部分州通过广播信息减少公众对乙型肝炎疫苗接种犹豫态度的效果。核心问题是广播信息是否能够提高公众对乙型肝炎疫苗接种的意识、信任度和疫苗接种意愿,特别是在错误信息、文化误解和难以获得可靠健康信息的背景下。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本研究采用调查研究设计,通过向选定州的居民发放结构化问卷收集数据。次级数据来源于广播节目档案和公共卫生报告。问卷回答通过简单百分比分析来量化公众在认知、知识和行为方面的趋势,次级数据则通过定性内容分析来评估信息框架、文化相关性和说服策略。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 研究发现,由于信息设计不佳、文化不匹配和说服内容薄弱,广播信息在减少公众对乙型肝炎疫苗接种的犹豫态度方面效果有限。这些因素限制了知识获取、信任建立和恐惧减少,从而维持了疫苗的犹豫态度。研究结果表明,在尼日利亚北中部各州,广播作为健康沟通工具在乙型肝炎疫苗接种相关情境下存在显著局限性。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 本研究指出了广播信息在应对公众犹豫态度方面的局限性,但未提供与其他沟通策略的比较数据。此外,未提及广播信息在不同人口群体中的效果差异,以及社会经济状况或教育水平等因素如何影响疫苗接种意愿。证据还缺乏关于广播信息对疫苗接种行为的长期影响的信息。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 本研究建议应仔细评估并重新设计广播信息,以确保其文化相关性、清晰度和具有说服力的内容,从而建立信任并减少恐惧。同时,广播电台和卫生部门应通过扩大覆盖范围至偏远地区、采用多种当地语言以及采用互动访谈节目和证言等吸引人的节目策略,来解决基础设施和受众相关的问题,以提高公众对乙型肝炎疫苗接种的接受度和接种率。

papers.abstract_zh: 乙型肝炎仍然是尼日利亚的主要公共卫生挑战,低疫苗接种接种率因广泛存在的公众犹豫态度而加剧,这种犹豫态度受到错误信息、文化误解以及难以获得可靠健康信息的影响,尤其是在北中部各州。应对这一挑战需要有效的健康沟通策略,以提高公众意识、信任度和疫苗接种意愿。本研究探讨了广播信息在减少公众对乙型肝炎疫苗接种犹豫态度方面的有效性,依据计划行为理论(Theory of Planned Behavior),该理论因其强调态度、主观规范和感知行为控制如何影响意图和健康相关决策而被采用。研究采用调查研究设计,通过结构化问卷收集了选定州居民的数据,并辅以从广播节目档案和公共卫生报告中获取的次级数据。问卷回答通过简单百分比分析来量化公众在认知、知识和行为方面的趋势,次级数据则通过定性内容分析来评估信息框架、文化相关性和说服策略。研究结果表明,广播信息的有效性受到信息设计不当、文化不匹配和说服内容薄弱等因素的严重影响,这些因素限制了知识获取、信任建立和恐惧减少,从而维持了疫苗的犹豫态度。此外,广播作为健康沟通工具的潜力受到基础设施限制、受众多样性、语言障碍、不足的节目策略以及缺乏社区参与的制约,这些因素降低了信息的传播范围、相关性和对疫苗接种决策的影响。研究建议应仔细评估并重新设计广播信息,以确保其文化相关性、清晰度和具有说服力的内容,从而建立信任并减少恐惧。同时,广播电台和卫生部门应通过扩大覆盖范围至偏远地区、采用多种当地语言以及采用互动访谈节目和证言等吸引人的节目策略,来解决基础设施和受众相关的问题,以提高公众对乙型肝炎疫苗接种的接受度和接种率。

papers.title: Genotypic variability and the mutational landscape of the hepatitis B virus among HIV‐infected patients living in the regions of Western Siberia (Russia)
papers.abstract: Abstract Background. Hepatitis B is a major public health problem due to its prevalence, complications, and genetic variability, which requires detailed molecular characterization for effective treatment. HIV‐HBV co‐infection exacerbates the course of hepatitis B, increases the risk of liver damage and death, and also reduces the effectiveness of antiviral therapy. The genetic diversity of the hepatitis B virus in HIV‐positive individuals has not been sufficiently studied, so such research is extremely important for developing more effective control and treatment strategies. Materials and methods. The study analyzed 708 blood serum samples were collected from patients with confirmed HIV infection. For primary screening for HBV DNA, a commercial "AmpliSens HBV-FL" kit was used. For the selected positive samples, next-generation sequencing on the Illumina MiSeq platform was used to obtain full-genomic HBV nucleotide sequences, which were serotyped, genotyped, and analyzed for the presence of clinically significant mutations Objective. To identify and characterize the variants of hepatitis B in HIV‐infected patients from three geographically close regions of Western Siberia (Novosibirsk Region, Tomsk Region, and the Altai Republic). The incidence of HBV genetic material in the study group was 8.5% (95% CI = 6.6–10.8). The work analyzed 60 full-genomic sequences of the identified HBV variants. All studied HBV variants were assigned to genotype D, and the distribution of HBV subgenotypes in the regions was different and consistent with previously obtained data. The overall detection rate of mutations in the hepatitis B virus surface antigen (S gene) was 55.0%, BCP mutations – 28.3%, PreCore mutations – 66.7%, mutations in the Core and X genes were detected in each of the 60 analyzed genome-wide sequences of HBV variants. The results highlight the importance of continuous molecular monitoring for the development of diagnostic strategies, improving the effectiveness of vaccination, and clinical management of HBV patients, especially among people living with HIV.

analysis.main_results: The overall detection rate of mutations in the hepatitis B virus surface antigen (S gene) was 55.0%, BCP mutations – 28.3%, PreCore mutations – 66.7%, and mutations in the Core and X genes were detected in each of the 60 analyzed genome-wide sequences of HBV variants.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the genotypic variability and mutational landscape of the hepatitis B virus (HBV) among HIV-infected patients in three regions of Western Siberia. The research aimed to characterize HBV variants in this population, as HBV genetic diversity is critical for effective treatment and management. A total of 708 blood serum samples were analyzed, with 8.5% testing positive for HBV. Of these, 60 full-genomic sequences were obtained and classified as genotype D. Mutations in the S gene, BCP, PreCore, Core, and X genes were detected in all sequences, with high prevalence in the Core and X genes. The study emphasizes the need for continuous molecular monitoring to improve diagnostic strategies and clinical care for HBV patients, especially those co-infected with HIV. While the findings are significant for understanding HBV dynamics in this specific population, the study's moderate confidence is due to its limited geographic scope and focus on a particular demographic group.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在识别和表征来自俄罗斯西西伯利亚地区三个地理相邻区域(新西伯利亚地区、托姆斯克地区和阿尔泰共和国)的HIV感染患者中的乙型肝炎病毒变异体。由于乙型肝炎病毒(乙型肝炎病毒)的患病率、并发症和遗传变异,乙型肝炎是主要的公共卫生问题,需要详细的分子特征分析以实现有效的治疗。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究分析了708份来自确诊HIV感染患者的血液清样本。在研究组中,HBV遗传物质的发病率为8.5%(95% CI = 6.6–10.8)。本研究分析了60个已鉴定HBV变异体的全基因组序列。
elements_zh.methods: 为了初步筛查HBV DNA,使用了商业化的"AmpliSens HBV-FL"试剂盒。对于筛选出的阳性样本,采用Illumina MiSeq平台的下一代测序技术获得完整的HBV基因组核苷酸序列,并进行血清型、基因型鉴定以及临床显著突变(突变)的分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 在乙型肝炎病毒表面抗原(S基因)中,突变的整体检出率为55.0%,BCP 突变为28.3%,PreCore 突变为66.7%,在60个分析的基因组全基因组序列中,Core和X基因中的突变均被检测到。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 结果强调了持续分子监测在诊断策略开发、提高疫苗接种效果以及HBV患者的临床管理中的重要性,尤其是在HIV感染者中。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为HBV患者的诊断策略、疫苗接种项目和临床管理方法的开发提供信息,特别是对于与HIV共感染的患者。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于研究的地理范围有限且专注于特定人群,本研究的置信度中等,但结果得到了对全基因组序列进行详细分子分析的支持。

analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study provides moderate confidence due to the limited geographic scope and the focus on a specific population, but the results are supported by detailed molecular analysis of full-genomic sequences.

papers.title_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒在俄罗斯西西伯利亚地区HIV感染患者中的基因型变异及突变图谱
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background. Hepatitis B is a major public health problem due to its prevalence, complications, and genetic variability, which requires detailed molecular characterization for effective treatment. HIV‐HBV co‐infection exacerbates the course of hepatitis B, increases the risk of liver damage and death, and also reduces the effectiveness of antiviral therapy. The genetic diversity of the hepatitis B virus in HIV‐positive individuals has not been sufficiently studied, so such research is extremely important for developing more effective control and treatment strategies. Materials and methods. The study analyzed 708 blood serum samples were collected from patients with confirmed HIV infection. For primary screening for HBV DNA, a commercial "AmpliSens HBV-FL" kit was used. For the selected positive samples, next-generation sequencing on the Illumina MiSeq platform was used to obtain full-genomic HBV nucleotide sequences, which were serotyped, genotyped, and analyzed for the presence of clinically significant mutations Objective. To identify and characterize the variants of hepatitis B in HIV‐infected patients from three geographically close regions of Western Siberia (Novosibirsk Region, Tomsk Region, and the Altai Republic). The incidence of HBV genetic material in the study group was 8.5% (95% CI = 6.6–10.8). The work analyzed 60 full-genomic sequences of the identified HBV variants. All studied HBV variants were assigned to genotype D, and the distribution of HBV subgenotypes in the regions was different and consistent with previously obtained data. The overall detection rate of mutations in the hepatitis B virus surface antigen (S gene) was 55.0%, BCP mutations – 28.3%, PreCore mutations – 66.7%, mutations in the Core and X genes were detected in each of the 60 analyzed genome-wide sequences of HBV variants. The results highlight the importance of continuous molecular monitoring for the development of diagnostic strategies, improving the effectiveness of vaccination, and clinical management of HBV patients, especially among people living with HIV.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景。由于乙型肝炎病毒(乙型肝炎病毒)的患病率、并发症和遗传变异,乙型肝炎是主要的公共卫生问题,需要详细的分子特征分析以实现有效的治疗。HIV与HBV的共感染会加剧乙型肝炎的病程,增加肝脏损伤和死亡的风险,同时也会降低抗病毒药物治疗的有效性。目前对HIV阳性个体中乙型肝炎病毒的遗传多样性研究尚不充分,因此此类研究对于开发更有效的控制和治疗策略具有极其重要的意义。材料和方法。本研究分析了708份来自确诊HIV感染患者的血液清样本。为了初步筛查HBV DNA,使用了商业化的"AmpliSens HBV-FL"试剂盒。对于筛选出的阳性样本,采用Illumina MiSeq平台的下一代测序技术获得完整的HBV基因组核苷酸序列,并进行血清型、基因型鉴定以及临床显著突变(突变)的分析。目的。识别和表征来自俄罗斯西西伯利亚地区三个地理相邻区域(新西伯利亚地区、托姆斯克地区和阿尔泰共和国)的HIV感染患者中的乙型肝炎病毒变异体。在研究组中,HBV遗传物质的发病率为8.5%(95% CI = 6.6–10.8)。本研究分析了60个已鉴定HBV变异体的全基因组序列。所有研究的HBV变异体均被归类为基因型D,且各地区的HBV亚基因型分布不同,与之前获得的数据一致。在乙型肝炎病毒表面抗原(S基因)中,突变的整体检出率为55.0%,BCP 突变为28.3%,PreCore 突变为66.7%,在60个分析的基因组全基因组序列中,Core和X基因中的突变均被检测到。结果强调了持续分子监测在诊断策略开发、提高疫苗接种效果以及HBV患者的临床管理中的重要性,尤其是在HIV感染者中。
