papers.title: Knowledge, Attitude and Practice Regarding Hepatitis-B Virus Infection among Slum Population of Dhaka City, Bangladesh
papers.abstract: Background: The Hepatitis B virus(HBV) infection is an important cause of mortality and morbidity in developing countries. Prevalence rate of HBV infection differs from country to country. In Bangladesh, there have been few small-scale studies on seroprevalence of HBV infection in selective class of people. But no population-based data is available to assess disease burden and draw large-scale intervention measure in slum area of Dhaka City. Objective: To assess knowledge, attitudes, and Practice regarding hepatitis B virus infection in a low-literacy urban population. Methods: This cross-sectional study was conducted to estimate to the knowledge, attitude and practices of slum people regarding viral hepatitis. The study was carried out among the 2000 adult slum population of Dhaka city, Bangladesh during the year July 2006 to June 2007. There are 4966 slum clusters in Dhaka city. Subjects’ selection from each cluster was by simple random sampling method. Trained interviewers were recruited for data collection with well-designed and structured validated questionnaires. After the collection of data, 3-5 ml of blood from each individual was drawn for HbsAg testing. The ELISA method confirmed HbsAg in cases where it was positive. Results: The majority of participants (82.57%) had general knowledge about hepatitis, but specific understanding was limited. Out of 2000 subjects 828 (41%) were male and 1172 (59%) were female. Mean (±SD) age was 31.91(±11.34) yrs. Among them 1062 (31.10%) were illiterate, 522 (26.10%) had primary level education; 318(15.9%), 54(2.7%) and 44(2.2%) were SSC, HSC and graduates respectively. They came from diverse occupations: house wife- 602 (30%), day laborer- 340 (17%) and industryworker-190(10%). Mean (±SD) house hold population size was 4.91(±2.13). Regarding knowledge of jaundice, a total of 1651(82.57%) had heard the name of jaundice and the rest of the population had not heard the name. Regarding the source of information about jaundice, 1529(76.45%) people had gained knowledge from other public and 262(13.12%) from electronic and print media. Only 16 (0.77%) had gathered knowledge from doctors and health workers. About the symptoms of jaundice, 1034(51.72%) said yellow coloration of urine, 276(13.78%) said yellow coloration of eye, 537(26.86%) said anorexia and 146(7.31%) had no knowledge. Among the study population 1081(54.05%) subjects had past history of jaundice. Regarding the knowledge about infective cause of jaundice, 1859(92.94%) had no knowledge. Only 7.06% knew HBV could be caused by an infectious agent, and 53.99% were unaware of transmission modes. Vaccination rates were low, with only 2.33% having received the HBV vaccine. Risk factors included receiving injections from unqualified providers (16.96%) and using disposable syringes (20.91%). Tobacco use (28.48%) and smoking (18.96%) were common addictions. Conclusion: Knowledge about viral hepatitis is poor in Dhaka City’s urban slums. Despite this, residents show interest in learning more and getting tested, though they prefer traditional healers over modern healthcare due to economic and educational constraints. Risk factors for HBV include overcrowding, young age, male sex, barbershop shaving, and low vaccination rates. These findings underscore the need for improved education, healthcare access, and targeted interventions in these communities.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding hepatitis B virus infection in a low-literacy urban population. The background highlights that HBV infection is a significant cause of mortality and morbidity in developing countries, with prevalence rates varying by country.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study was conducted among 2000 adult slum residents in Dhaka City, Bangladesh, from July 2006 to June 2007. The population was selected through simple random sampling from 4966 slum clusters in the city.
analysis.methods: Trained interviewers collected data using validated questionnaires. Blood samples were taken from each participant for HbsAg testing, and the ELISA method confirmed positive cases.
analysis.main_results: 82.57% of participants had general knowledge about hepatitis, but specific understanding was limited. Only 7.06% knew HBV could be caused by an infectious agent, and 53.99% were unaware of transmission modes. Additionally, 2.33% had received the HBV vaccine.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that knowledge about viral hepatitis is poor in Dhaka City’s urban slums, despite residents showing interest in learning more and getting tested.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the need for improved education and healthcare access in these communities to address the poor knowledge and low vaccination rates related to HBV infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on self-reported data and the potential for recall bias. The evidence is moderate as it provides descriptive data on knowledge and risk factors but lacks longitudinal or causal analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection among the slum population of Dhaka City, Bangladesh. It found that while 82.57% of participants had general knowledge about hepatitis, specific understanding of HBV causes and transmission modes was limited. Only 2.33% had received the HBV vaccine, and risk factors included low literacy, economic constraints, and limited access to healthcare. The authors concluded that knowledge about viral hepatitis is poor in these communities, emphasizing the need for improved education and healthcare access. The study's cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported data limit the strength of the evidence, which is considered moderate.

These findings underscore the need for improved education, healthcare access, and targeted interventions in these communities.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染是发展中国家肝硬化和发病率的重要原因。HBV感染的患病率因国家而异。在孟加拉国,针对特定人群的HBV感染研究较少,但目前尚无基于人口的数据来评估贫民区的疾病负担并制定大规模干预措施。目的:评估低文化水平城市人群中对乙型肝炎病毒感染的知识、态度和实践。方法:本横断面研究旨在估计贫民区居民对病毒性肝炎的知识、态度和实践。研究在2006年7月至2007年6月期间,针对孟加拉国达卡市的2000名成年贫民区居民进行。达卡市共有4966个贫民区聚类,每个聚类通过简单随机抽样方法选择受试者。招募了经过培训的访谈员,使用经过良好设计和结构验证的问卷进行数据收集。在收集数据后,从每位受试者身上抽取3-5毫升血液进行HBsAg检测。ELISA方法确认了HBsAg阳性病例。结果:大多数参与者(82.57%)对肝炎有一般性了解,但具体理解有限。在2000名受试者中,828名(41%)为男性,1172名(59%)为女性。平均(±SD)年龄为31.91(±11.34)岁。其中1062名(31.10%)为文盲,522名(26.10%)接受过小学教育;318名(15.9%)、54名(2.7%)和44名(2.2%)分别接受过中等教育、高中教育和大学教育。他们的职业多样:家庭主妇602名(30%),日工340名(17%),工业工人190名(10%)。平均(±SD)家庭人口规模为4.91(±2.13)。关于黄疸的知识,共有1651名(82.57%)参与者听说过黄疸这个名字,其余的人则没有。关于黄疸信息的来源,1529名(76.45%)参与者通过其他公共渠道获得知识,262名(13.12%)通过电子和印刷媒体获得知识。仅有16名(0.77%)参与者从医生和卫生工作者处获得知识。关于黄疸的症状,1034名(51.72%)参与者提到尿液变黄,276名(13.78%)提到眼睛变黄,537名(26.86%)提到食欲不振,146名(7.31%)则没有相关知识。在研究人群中,1081名(54.05%)有黄疸的既往病史。关于黄疸的感染原因,1859名(92.94%)参与者没有相关知识。仅有7.06%的参与者知道HBV是由传染性病原体引起的,而53.99%的参与者不了解传播方式。疫苗接种率较低,仅有2.33%的参与者接种过HBV疫苗。风险因素包括从非合格提供者处接受注射(16.96%)和使用一次性针头(20.91%)。烟草使用(28.48%)和吸烟(18.96%)是常见的成瘾行为。结论:达卡市城市贫民区对病毒性肝炎的知识较为匮乏。尽管如此,居民表现出学习更多知识和接受检测的兴趣,但由于经济和教育限制,他们更倾向于选择传统治疗者而非现代医疗。HBV的风险因素包括拥挤、年轻年龄、男性性别、理发店刮脸以及疫苗接种率低。这些发现强调了在这些社区中改善教育、医疗可及性和针对性干预的必要性。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估低文化水平城市人群中对乙型肝炎病毒感染的知识、态度和实践。背景指出,HBV感染是发展中国家肝硬化和发病率的重要原因,其患病率因国家而异。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本横断面研究在孟加拉国达卡市的2000名成年贫民区居民中进行,时间为2006年7月至2007年6月。该人群通过简单随机抽样方法从达卡市的4966个贫民区聚类中选取。
analysis_zh.methods: 经过培训的访谈员使用经过验证的问卷收集数据。从每位参与者身上抽取血液样本进行HBsAg检测,并通过ELISA方法确认阳性病例。
analysis_zh.main_results: 82.57%的参与者对肝炎有一般性了解,但具体理解有限。仅有7.06%的参与者知道HBV是由传染性病原体引起的,而53.99%的参与者不了解传播方式。此外,2.33%的参与者接种过HBV疫苗。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出结论,达卡市城市贫民区对病毒性肝炎的知识较为匮乏,尽管居民表现出学习更多知识和接受检测的兴趣。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了在这些社区中改善教育和医疗可及性的必要性,以应对与HBV感染相关的知识匮乏和疫苗接种率低的问题。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于依赖于自我报告数据,可能存在回忆偏差。证据强度中等,因为它提供了关于知识和风险因素的描述性数据,但缺乏纵向或因果分析。

papers.title: Awareness and Preventive Practices of Hepatitis B Virus Infection Among Pregnant Women in Bangladesh
papers.abstract: Background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a major global health challenge, particularly concerning for pregnant women due to the risk of vertical transmission. Although vaccines and antiviral therapies are available, public awareness and preventive practices in Bangladesh remain insufficient. Objective: This study aimed to examine the relationship between awareness and preventive practices of HBV infection among pregnant women in Bangladesh. Methods: A descriptive correlational study design was conducted at the 250-Bedded General Hospital in Kushtia. A total of 112 pregnant women were selected through a convenience sampling technique. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews using structured questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics. Results: The study found that 80.4% of participants demonstrated limited awareness regarding disease transmission, symptoms, screening procedures, and vaccination. Furthermore, 75% of participants reported insufficient engagement in preventive practices. These findings highlight a substantial deficiency in both awareness and implementation of preventive behaviors. Socio-demographic variables, including educational level, occupation, monthly family income, and place of residence, were significantly associated with awareness and preventive practices. Conclusion: Awareness of HBV infection among pregnant women was inadequate, and their preventive practices were also limited. Therefore, comprehensive health education programs are recommended to be implemented during antenatal visits to increase awareness and improve preventive behaviors among pregnant women in Bangladesh.
papers.journal: International Journal of Maternal Perinatal and Neonatal Care

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染是全球主要的公共卫生挑战,尤其对孕妇而言,由于存在垂直传播的风险。尽管疫苗和抗病毒药物疗法已可用,但孟加拉国公众对HBV感染的认知和预防措施仍显不足。目的:本研究旨在探讨孟加拉国孕妇对HBV感染的认知与预防措施之间的关系。方法:在Kushtia的250床综合医院进行了一项描述性相关性研究,通过便利抽样方法选取了112名孕妇。数据通过面对面访谈和结构化问卷收集,并使用描述性和推断性统计方法进行分析。结果:研究发现,80.4%的参与者对疾病传播、症状、筛查程序和疫苗接种的认知有限。此外,75%的参与者报告称在预防措施上的参与不足。这些发现突显了孟加拉国孕妇在认知和预防行为实施方面存在显著的不足。社会人口学变量,包括教育水平、职业、月家庭收入和居住地,与认知和预防措施显著相关。结论:孟加拉国孕妇对HBV感染的认知不足,其预防措施也有限。因此,建议在产前检查期间实施全面的健康教育项目,以提高孕妇对HBV感染的认知并改善其预防行为。

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Health sciences students are at risk of occupational exposure to blood-borne pathogens, including hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). The aim of this study was to evaluate the knowledge, awareness, attitudes, preventive practices and occupational exposure of health sciences students in Taiz, Yemen. Methods A descriptive analytical cross sectional study was carried on 505 health sciences students in five universities in Taiz, Yemen from September 2025 to July 2026. The sampling method for the participants was stratified sampling, based on university, discipline and academic year. A self-administered, structured questionnaire was used to collect data, which included knowledge, attitudes, preventive practices, vaccination status for HBV, and occupational exposure. Data analysis was done using descriptive statistics and Pearson's chi square tests in SPSS statistics. Results Mean knowledge score was 6.14 ± 1.98 out of 10, 50.7% of students had good knowledge. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the knowledge, awareness, attitudes, preventive practices and occupational exposure of health sciences students in Taiz, Yemen regarding hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).
analysis.study_design_and_population: A descriptive analytical cross-sectional study was conducted on 505 health sciences students across five universities in Taiz, Yemen from September 2025 to July 2026.
analysis.methods: Stratified sampling was used to select participants based on university, discipline, and academic year. Data were collected using a self-administered, structured questionnaire that assessed knowledge, attitudes, preventive practices, vaccination status for HBV, and occupational exposure.
analysis.main_results: The mean knowledge score was 6.14 ± 1.98 out of 10, with 50.7% of students having good knowledge. Students at the clinical stage had higher good knowledge rates compared to pre-clinical students (57.0% vs.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight a significant knowledge gap among health sciences students, particularly in pre-clinical stages, and suggest the need for targeted educational interventions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results can inform the development of educational programs to improve HBV awareness and preventive practices among health sciences students, which is critical for reducing occupational transmission risks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and self-reported data, which may introduce bias. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed the knowledge and awareness of health sciences students in Taiz, Yemen, regarding hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). A descriptive analytical cross-sectional study was conducted on 505 students across five universities from September 2025 to July 2026, using stratified sampling and a self-administered questionnaire. The mean knowledge score was 6.14 ± 1.98 out of 10, with 50.7% of students demonstrating good knowledge. Clinical-stage students had higher good knowledge rates than pre-clinical students (57.0% vs. 34.0%, p < 0.05). The authors interpreted these findings as highlighting a significant knowledge gap, particularly among pre-clinical students, and emphasized the need for targeted educational interventions. The study's results can inform the development of educational programs to improve HBV awareness and preventive practices among health sciences students, which is essential for reducing occupational transmission risks. However, the study is limited by its cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported data, which may introduce bias, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

The aim of this study was to evaluate the knowledge, awareness, attitudes, preventive practices and occupational exposure of health sciences students in Taiz, Yemen. papers.title: Post-vaccination immunity to hepatitis B virus in medical personnel: predictive modeling, key predictors, and risk management
papers.abstract: Objective : to analyze the post-vaccination immune response to hepatitis B virus in medical personnel to determine prognostic criteria and risk management. Materials and methods : the results of serological screening of 1,380 employees of a multidisciplinary medical center for anti-HBsAg, HBsAg in 2024-2025 and their vaccination history data were analyzed. Laboratory tests were performed on the basis of the laboratory of the European Medical Center “UMMC-Health” by enzyme immunoassay using a set of reagents “Vecto HBsAg-antibodies”, JSC “Vector-Best”. The protective concentration of specific antibodies in the blood serum was considered to be 10 mIU/ml or more. Statistical processing was performed in Microsoft Office Excel 2016 and SPSS Statistics (v. Results: in 81.8% of the employees, the concentration of anti-HBsAg was more than 10 mIU/ml. When constructing a binary logistic regression model (p<0,001), it was found that increasing the age of employees by 1 year lowered the chances of a positive result by 1,052 times. An increase in the period since the last injection of the vaccine for each year reduced the chances of a positive result by 1,055 times. Administration of each additional dose of the vaccine increased the chances of a positive result by 2,036 times. The sensitivity of the model was 73.9%, and the specificity was 73.7%. The overall diagnostic significance of the model is 73.8%. Conclusion : the results of the study indicate the need for further study of the feasibility of booster immunization of medical workers, taking into account a comprehensive assessment of humoral and cellular immunity, in order to effectively manage biological risks.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to analyze the post-vaccination immune response to hepatitis B virus in medical personnel to determine prognostic criteria and risk management.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed serological screening results of 1,380 employees from a multidisciplinary medical center for anti-HBsAg and HBsAg in 2024-2025, along with their vaccination history data.
analysis.methods: Laboratory tests were conducted using enzyme immunoassay with the reagent set “Vecto HBsAg-antibodies” from JSC “Vector-Best”. A binary logistic regression model was constructed to identify predictors of positive immune response.
analysis.main_results: In 81.8% of the employees, the concentration of anti-HBsAg was more than 10 mIU/ml. Increasing age by 1 year lowered the chances of a positive result by 1,052 times. An increase in the period since the last injection of the vaccine for each year reduced the chances of a positive result by 1,055 times. Administration of each additional dose of the vaccine increased the chances of a positive result by 2,036 times. The model had a sensitivity of 73.9% and specificity of 73.7%, with an overall diagnostic significance of 73.8%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating the need for further study on the feasibility of booster immunization for medical workers, considering a comprehensive assessment of humoral and cellular immunity to effectively manage biological risks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of targeted booster immunization strategies for medical personnel to enhance post-vaccination immunity and reduce the risk of hepatitis B virus exposure.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on serological data and a binary logistic regression model, which may not fully capture the complexity of immune responses. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and potential confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the post-vaccination immune response to hepatitis B virus in medical personnel, focusing on predictive modeling and key predictors. It analyzed serological screening data from 1,380 employees over 2024-2025, using enzyme immunoassay to measure anti-HBsAg levels. The results showed that 81.8% of employees had antibody concentrations above 10 mIU/ml, with age, time since last vaccination, and number of doses significantly affecting the likelihood of a positive result. The model demonstrated moderate sensitivity and specificity, suggesting its potential utility in risk management. The authors concluded that further research on booster immunization, incorporating both humoral and cellular immunity assessments, is necessary to improve hepatitis B virus risk management strategies in medical settings.

papers.title: Serum CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 levels in treatment-naive chronic hepatitis B: associations with EASL-based clinical phenotypes, histological inflammatory activity, and non-invasive fibrosis indices
papers.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) is a major global health issue, as ongoing viral replication can drive hepatic inflammation and immune dysregulation, increasing the risk of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. CXCL-10, a proinflammatory chemokine, and CTLA-4, an inhibitory immune checkpoint, may each capture a different facet of the immune response in CHB. This study evaluated serum CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 in CHB patients and their associations with HBV DNA, laboratory findings, and non-invasive fibrosis markers. In total, 86 individuals were enrolled: 21 healthy controls and 65 treatment-naive CHB patients. CHB patients were categorized by HBV DNA level into ≤ 105 IU/mL ( n = 33) and > 105 IU/mL ( n = 32). Patients were also classified into EASL (European Association for the Study of the Liver)-based clinical phenotypes using HBeAg status, HBV DNA, and ALT. Liver biopsy data (Ishak fibrosis stage and modified Ishak HAI score) were available for 43 patients (66.2%). FIB-4 was calculated for all participants. Serum CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 were measured by ELISA, and laboratory-based inflammatory and fibrosis-related indices were calculated. Group comparisons and correlation analyses were used to assess associations; ROC analyses were descriptive and exploratory. Serum levels of CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 differed significantly among study groups and were highest in patients with elevated viral loads (both p < 0.001). Viral load correlated strongly with CXCL-10 ( r = 0.786) and CTLA-4 ( r = 0.559), and CXCL-10 correlated strongly with CTLA-4 ( r = 0.690; all p < 0.001). Both CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 correlated more strongly with the modified Ishak HAI score ( r = 0.519 and r = 0.509, respectively; p < 0.001) than with fibrosis stage. CXCL-10 levels were elevated in Phase 2 (HBeAg-positive chronic hepatitis) compared to Phase 3 ( p < 0.001) and Phase 4 ( p = 0.005). The descriptive ROC performance was moderate (AUC 0.78 for CXCL-10; 0.76 for CTLA-4, sensitivity 47%); in an exploratory analysis, CXCL-10 differentiated high (HAI ≥ 7) from low histological activity (AUC 0.77). Serum CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 were associated with HBV DNA, biochemical liver injury, and histological inflammatory activity in treatment-naive CHB, correlating more strongly with the modified Ishak HAI score than with fibrosis stage. These findings suggest a role for CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 as markers of inflammatory and immunoregulatory activity in CHB, warranting confirmation in larger, longitudinal cohorts.

papers.title_zh: 治疗初发者慢性乙型肝炎: 与基于EASL的临床表型、组织学炎症活动度及非侵入性纤维化指标相关的血清CXCL-10和CTLA-4水平
papers.source_body_en: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) is a major global health issue, as ongoing viral replication can drive hepatic inflammation and immune dysregulation, increasing the risk of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. CXCL-10, a proinflammatory chemokine, and CTLA-4, an inhibitory immune checkpoint, may each capture a different facet of the immune response in CHB. This study evaluated serum CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 in CHB patients and their associations with HBV DNA, laboratory findings, and non-invasive fibrosis markers. In total, 86 individuals were enrolled: 21 healthy controls and 65 treatment-naive CHB patients. CHB patients were categorized by HBV DNA level into ≤ 105 IU/mL ( n = 33) and > 105 IU/mL ( n = 32). Patients were also classified into EASL (European Association for the Study of the Liver)-based clinical phenotypes using HBeAg status, HBV DNA, and ALT. Liver biopsy data (Ishak fibrosis stage and modified Ishak HAI score) were available for 43 patients (66.2%). FIB-4 was calculated for all participants. Serum CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 were measured by ELISA, and laboratory-based inflammatory and fibrosis-related indices were calculated. Group comparisons and correlation analyses were used to assess associations; ROC analyses were descriptive and exploratory. Serum levels of CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 differed significantly among study groups and were highest in patients with elevated viral loads (both p < 0.001). Viral load correlated strongly with CXCL-10 ( r = 0.786) and CTLA-4 ( r = 0.559), and CXCL-10 correlated strongly with CTLA-4 ( r = 0.690; all p < 0.001). Both CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 correlated more strongly with the modified Ishak HAI score ( r = 0.519 and r = 0.509, respectively; p < 0.001) than with fibrosis stage. CXCL-10 levels were elevated in Phase 2 (HBeAg-positive chronic hepatitis) compared to Phase 3 ( p < 0.001) and Phase 4 ( p = 0.005). The descriptive ROC performance was moderate (AUC 0.78 for CXCL-10; 0.76 for CTLA-4, sensitivity 47%); in an exploratory analysis, CXCL-10 differentiated high (HAI ≥ 7) from low histological activity (AUC 0.77). Serum CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 were associated with HBV DNA, biochemical liver injury, and histological inflammatory activity in treatment-naive CHB, correlating more strongly with the modified Ishak HAI score than with fibrosis stage. These findings suggest a role for CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 as markers of inflammatory and immunoregulatory activity in CHB, warranting confirmation in larger, longitudinal cohorts.
papers.abstract_zh: 慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)是全球主要的健康问题,因为持续的病毒复制可驱动肝炎和免疫失调,增加肝硬化和肝细胞癌的风险。CXCL-10是一种促炎性趋化因子,而CTLA-4是一种抑制性免疫检查点,它们可能分别反映慢性乙型肝炎中不同的方面。本研究评估了慢性乙型肝炎患者血清CXCL-10和CTLA-4水平及其与HBV DNA、实验室检查结果和非侵入性纤维化标志物之间的关联。共纳入86名受试者:21名健康对照者和65名治疗初发的慢性乙型肝炎患者。根据HBV DNA水平,将慢性乙型肝炎患者分为≤105 IU/mL(n=33)和>105 IU/mL(n=32)两组。患者还根据HBeAg状态、HBV DNA和ALT水平被分为基于EASL(欧洲肝脏研究协会)的临床表型。43名患者(66.2%)提供了肝脏活检数据(Ishak纤维化分期和改良Ishak HAI评分)。对所有参与者计算了FIB-4。通过ELISA检测血清CXCL-10和CTLA-4水平,并计算了基于实验室的炎症和纤维化相关指标。通过组间比较和相关性分析评估了这些关联;ROC分析为描述性和探索性分析。血清CXCL-10和CTLA-4水平在不同研究组间存在显著差异,且在病毒载量升高的患者中最高(两者p<0.001)。病毒载量与CXCL-10(r=0.786)和CTLA-4(r=0.559)呈强相关,而CXCL-10与CTLA-4也呈强相关(r=0.690;所有p<0.001)。CXCL-10和CTLA-4与改良Ishak HAI评分的相关性(分别为r=0.519和r=0.509;p<0.001)强于与纤维化分期的相关性。与Phase 3(p=0.005)和Phase 4相比,Phase 2(HBeAg阳性慢性肝炎)患者的CXCL-10水平升高(p<0.001)。描述性ROC分析的性能中等(CXCL-10的AUC为0.78;CTLA-4的AUC为0.76,灵敏度为47%);在探索性分析中,CXCL-10可区分高(HAI≥7)与低组织学活动(AUC为0.77)。血清CXCL-10和CTLA-4水平与治疗初发的慢性乙型肝炎患者的HBV DNA、生化肝损伤及组织学炎症活动度相关,且与改良Ishak HAI评分的相关性强于与纤维化分期的相关性。这些发现表明,CXCL-10和CTLA-4可能作为慢性乙型肝炎中炎症和免疫调节活动的标志物,需要在更大规模、纵向研究中进行验证。

papers.title: SEROLOGICAL CLEARANCE OF HBSAG IN CHRONIC HEPATITIS B: EXPERIENCE IN A UNIVERSITY HOSPITAL
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection represents a major public health problem due to its high morbidity and mortality associated with liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Functional cure, characterized by serological clearance of the HBV surface antigen (HBsAg), is the main therapeutic goal, since sterilizing viral eradication is not yet feasible. HBsAg clearance rates vary widely in the literature, and understanding the factors associated with this event is crucial for optimizing patient management. Objective: To investigate the HBsAg clearance rate and identify the demographic, clinical, and virological factors associated with this event in a cohort of patients with chronic hepatitis B virus infection followed up at a reference center in Northeast Brazil. Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted through a review of the medical records of patients with chronic hepatitis B virus infection treated at a Hepatology Service in Northeast Brazil between January 2015 and October 2025. Clinical, demographic and laboratory variables were analyzed. Statistical analysis used tests such as Mann-Whitney for quantitative variables and Fisher’s exact test for categorical variables, in addition to the construction of Kaplan-Meier curves with the Log-Rank test to evaluate HBsAg clearance. The significance level was set at P<0.05. Results: Of the 600 medical records screened, 299 patients were included in the analysis, 63.2% of whom were women, with a median age of 45 years. During a mean follow-up period of 5.14 years, totaling 1,538 person-years, 12 patients (4%) achieved serological clearance of HBsAg, resulting in an annual rate of 0.78%. Statistical analysis revealed significant associations between HBsAg clearance and advanced age (P=0.008) and lower HBV-DNA levels (P=0.0156). Conclusion: The annual rate of HBsAg serological clearance in this cohort was 0.78%. Advanced age and low viral load levels were significantly associated with functional cure. These findings enrich the knowledge about the natural history of chronic hepatitis B in the region and reaffirm the importance of viral suppression in disease control.

papers.title_zh: 慢性乙型肝炎病毒血清学清除:巴西东北部大学医院的经验
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Background: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection represents a major public health problem due to its high morbidity and mortality associated with liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Functional cure, characterized by serological clearance of the HBV surface antigen (HBsAg), is the main therapeutic goal, since sterilizing viral eradication is not yet feasible. HBsAg clearance rates vary widely in the literature, and understanding the factors associated with this event is crucial for optimizing patient management. Objective: To investigate the HBsAg clearance rate and identify the demographic, clinical, and virological factors associated with this event in a cohort of patients with chronic hepatitis B virus infection followed up at a reference center in Northeast Brazil. Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted through a review of the medical records of patients with chronic hepatitis B virus infection treated at a Hepatology Service in Northeast Brazil between January 2015 and October 2025. Clinical, demographic and laboratory variables were analyzed. Statistical analysis used tests such as Mann-Whitney for quantitative variables and Fisher’s exact test for categorical variables, in addition to the construction of Kaplan-Meier curves with the Log-Rank test to evaluate HBsAg clearance. The significance level was set at P<0.05. Results: Of the 600 medical records screened, 299 patients were included in the analysis, 63.2% of whom were women, with a median age of 45 years. During a mean follow-up period of 5.14 years, totaling 1,538 person-years, 12 patients (4%) achieved serological clearance of HBsAg, resulting in an annual rate of 0.78%. Statistical analysis revealed significant associations between HBsAg clearance and advanced age (P=0.008) and lower HBV-DNA levels (P=0.0156). Conclusion: The annual rate of HBsAg serological clearance in this cohort was 0.78%. Advanced age and low viral load levels were significantly associated with functional cure. These findings enrich the knowledge about the natural history of chronic hepatitis B in the region and reaffirm the importance of viral suppression in disease control.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景:慢性乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染由于其高发病率以及与肝硬化和肝细胞癌相关的特性,构成了重大的公共卫生问题。功能性治愈,以HBV表面抗原(HBsAg)的血清学清除为特征,是主要的治疗目标,因为目前尚无法实现病毒的完全清除。HBsAg清除率在文献中存在较大差异,了解与这一事件相关的因素对于优化患者管理至关重要。目的:探讨慢性乙型肝炎病毒感染患者在巴西东北部参考中心随访的队列研究中HBsAg清除率,并识别与该事件相关的流行病学、临床和病毒学因素。方法:通过回顾2015年1月至2025年10月期间在巴西东北部某肝病科治疗的慢性乙型肝炎病毒感染患者的医疗记录,进行了一项回顾性队列研究研究。分析了临床、人口统计学和实验室变量。统计分析采用Mann-Whitney检验用于定量变量,Fisher精确检验用于分类变量,同时构建Kaplan-Meier曲线并使用Log-Rank检验评估HBsAg清除情况。显著性水平设定为P<0.05。结果:在筛选的600份医疗记录中,有299名患者被纳入分析,其中63.2%为女性,中位年龄为45岁。在平均随访期5.14年,总计1,538人年的观察中,12名患者(4%)实现了HBsAg的血清学清除,年清除率为0.78%。统计分析显示,HBsAg清除与年龄较大(P=0.008)和较低的HBV-DNA水平(P=0.0156)存在显著关联。结论:在该队列研究中,HBsAg血清学清除的年发生率为0.78%。年龄较大和病毒载量较低与功能性治愈显著相关。这些发现丰富了该地区慢性乙型肝炎病毒自然史的知识,并重申了病毒抑制在疾病控制中的重要性。

papers.title: Depression and medication adherence among chronic hepatitis B patients receiving resilience-based care versus standard care during antiviral therapy: a retrospective cohort study
papers.abstract: Objective To evaluate the association between receiving a resilience-focused program in addition to standard care and depressive symptoms and medication adherence among patients with CHB receiving antiviral therapy. Methods In this retrospective cohort study, 200 patients diagnosed with CHB and treated at our hospital's hepatology clinic between July 2022 and June 2025 were included. Based on historical records, 100 patients who voluntarily completed a structured 12-week resilience promotion program in addition to standard care formed the observation group, and 100 patients who received standard care only formed the control group. Primary outcomes at the 6-month follow-up were depressive symptom severity measured by the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) and medication adherence measured by the Medication Possession Ratio (MPR). Secondary outcomes included resilience (Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale-10, CD-RISC-10), virological response, alanine aminotransferase (ALT) normalization, quality of life (SF-36), adverse events, and healthcare utilization. To account for potential confounding by indication and baseline imbalances, multivariable linear, logistic, and Poisson regression models were used, with adjusted effect estimates and 95% confidence intervals reported. Results At the 6-month follow-up, the observation group had lower depression scores (6.78 ± 3.45 vs. 10.23 ± 4.12), higher MPR (0.92 ± 0.08 vs. 0.78 ± 0.15), and higher resilience scores (32.45 ± 5.67 vs. Virological response (85.0% vs. 70.0%; adjusted OR 2.46, 95% CI 1.35 to 4.48) and ALT normalization (80.0% vs. 65.0%; adjusted OR 2.01, 95% CI 1.10 to 3.67) were more frequent in the observation group. SF-36 physical and mental component scores were also higher in the observation group. Adverse event incidence was similar between groups. The observation group had fewer unplanned outpatient visits ( P = 0.045), and Poisson regression confirmed fewer outpatient visits in the observation group (adjusted rate ratio 0.72, 95% CI 0.56 to 0.93). However, because allocation was non-randomized, these associations may be affected by self-selection and residual confounding. Conclusion In this retrospective cohort study, receiving a resilience-focused program in addition to standard care was associated with lower depressive symptoms, better medication adherence, and more favorable virological and biochemical outcomes in patients with CHB.

papers.title: Near-Full-Length Hepatitis B Virus Genomes Isolated from Cerebrospinal Fluid of People Living with HIV and Cryptococcal Meningitis in Botswana
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Increasing evidence suggests that the hepatitis B virus (HBV) can be detected in extrahepatic compartments. Data on the molecular characteristics of HBV in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) remain limited, particularly among people living with HIV (PLWH) and cryptococcal meningitis (CM). This study aimed to characterize HBV genomes from plasma and CSF and compare paired sequences for genetic similarity and potential compartment-specific differences. Methods: Archived plasma and CSF samples from PLWH with CM from Botswana enrolled in AMBITION-CM trial (2018–2021) were sequenced using Oxford Nanopore Technology to generate near-full-length HBV genomes. Genotyping and mutational analysis were performed and paired plasma–CSF sequences were compared. Results: Four sequences were generated, including one plasma–CSF pair and two CSF-only sequences. The sequences clustered with genotypes A1 and D3. The single paired plasma–CSF sequences shared 98.8% nucleotide similarity, and clustered together with strong phylogenetic support (SH-aLRT/ultrafast bootstrap = 99.6/100). Variant analysis identified 492 and 545 high-quality variants (Q ≥ 30) in plasma and CSF, respectively. In the single paired sequences, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC)-associated mutation T1858C was detected in plasma but not in the CSF. Mutations were also identified in CSF-derived sequences, including A1762T/G1764A, G1896A, G1899A, associated with increased HCC risk, rtS184L, rtF194L, rtP236T, linked to antiviral resistance and sP127L, sQ129L, sM133L, sS136P, associated with immune escape. Conclusions: Near-full-length HBV genomes were successfully recovered and genetically characterized from the CSF of PLWH with CM. The single plasma–CSF paired sample, showed high genetic similarity and had a compartment-specific mutation. Clinically relevant mutations were observed in the CSF warranting further investigation of HBV in the CSF to confirm these observations in PLWH with CM. These preliminary findings from a limited number of participants provide a basis for larger-scale studies of near-full-length HBV genome characterization in CSF.

Methods: Archived plasma and CSF samples from PLWH with CM from Botswana enrolled in AMBITION-CM trial (2018–2021) were sequenced using Oxford Nanopore Technology to generate near-full-length HBV genomes. Genotyping and mutational analysis were performed and paired plasma–CSF sequences were compared. Results: Four sequences were generated, including one plasma–CSF pair and two CSF-only sequences. The sequences clustered with genotypes A1 and D3. The single paired plasma–CSF sequences shared 98.8% nucleotide similarity, and clustered together with strong phylogenetic support (SH-aLRT/ultrafast bootstrap = 99.6/100). Variant analysis identified 492 and 545 high-quality variants (Q ≥ 30) in plasma and CSF, respectively. In the single paired sequences, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC)-associated mutation T1858C was detected in plasma but not in the CSF. Mutations were also identified in CSF-derived sequences, including A1762T/G1764A, G1896A, G1899A, associated with increased HCC risk, rtS184L, rtF194L, rtP236T, linked to antiviral resistance and sP127L, sQ129L, sM133L, sS136P, associated with immune escape. Conclusions: Near-full-length HBV genomes were successfully recovered and genetically characterized from the CSF of PLWH with CM. The single plasma–CSF paired sample, showed high genetic similarity and had a compartment-specific mutation. Clinically relevant mutations were observed in the CSF warranting further investigation of HBV in the CSF to confirm these observations in PLWH with CM. These preliminary findings from a limited number of participants provide a basis for larger-scale studies of near-full-length HBV genome characterization in CSF.

papers.title: The core obstacles and immunological mechanisms in the study of functional cure for Chronic Hepatitis B
papers.abstract: Attaining a functional cure constitutes the paramount therapeutic objective in the management of chronic hepatitis B (CHB), as it markedly reduces the incidence of hepatocellular carcinoma and the progression to terminal liver disease. Despite this, the current functional cure rate among CHB patients remains below 30%. Major impediments to achieving this outcome include the persistent existence of viral covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA), integration of the viral genome into the host’s DNA, immune tolerance resulting from prolonged exposure to elevated viral antigen levels, and host-mediated HBV-specific immune exhaustion and dysfunction at multiple regulatory levels. A thorough elucidation of the molecular pathways underpinning these barriers, alongside their associated immune regulatory networks, is critical for the advancement of novel therapeutic strategies. This review comprehensively integrates recent progress in understanding the virological mechanisms responsible for HBV persistence, host immune responses to HBV infection, and emerging immunotherapeutic interventions. The aim is to establish a theoretical foundation and provide critical perspectives to support the clinical translation of approaches designed to achieve a functional cure for CHB.

It highlights the persistent obstacles such as viral covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA), immune tolerance, and host-mediated immune exhaustion. The review integrates recent findings on virological mechanisms, host immune responses, and immunotherapeutic interventions to provide a theoretical foundation for future clinical applications. It emphasizes the need for a deeper understanding of molecular pathways and immune regulatory networks to develop effective therapeutic strategies. The review also outlines the importance of translating these insights into practical approaches for the treatment of CHB.

papers.title: Biological interpretation of baseline hepatitis B surface antigen and cirrhosis in determining interferon treatment duration
papers.abstract: The recent identification of baseline hepatitis B surface antigen and cirrhosis as independent predictors of extended interferon therapy provides a valuable clinical framework, yet the biological mechanisms underlying these associations require further elucidation. In this opinion review, we interpret these factors not merely as statistical covariates but as pathological surrogates for the virus-host equilibrium. We propose that high baseline hepatitis B surface antigen may reflect a deeply entrenched intrahepatic viral reservoir and may create an antigen-rich environment that impairs effective antiviral immunity. Concurrently, cirrhosis may be better understood as a spectrum of architectural remodeling in which vascular changes and sinusoidal defenestration could limit immune surveillance and affect local therapeutic access. Consequently, treatment durations exceeding 48 weeks may be required, at least in part, to overcome these profound immunological and structural barriers. We advocate shifting future predictive modeling from binary clinical definitions to a granular integration of viral kinetics and histological morphology to refine precision medicine in chronic hepatitis B.

papers.title: Novel HEP-FIB score combined with machine learning models for non-invasive prediction of significant hepatic fibrosis in chronic hepatitis B patients: a single-center, internally validated study
papers.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major global health burden. Assessment of hepatic fibrosis is important for risk stratification and guiding treatment in CHB. Liver biopsy, the reference standard for fibrosis staging, is invasive, and fraught with potential complications, creating the need for alternative non-invasive tools. Existing non-invasive fibrosis scores demonstrate variable diagnostic accuracy, and the role of lipids in fibrosis prediction remains insufficiently explored. We developed and internally validated HEP-FIB, a parsimonious score based on routinely available laboratory parameters, and evaluated machine learning (ML) models for non-invasive prediction of significant hepatic fibrosis in CHB patients. A retrospective cohort of 382 CHB patients was analyzed. Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression followed by multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of fibrosis. A novel HEP-FIB score was developed based on platelet count, liver function parameters, and lipid biomarkers. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, bootstrap internal validation and calibration analysis. The performance of HEP-FIB was compared with established non-invasive indices, including APRI, FIB-4, and GPR. In addition, ten ML algorithms were constructed and evaluated for predictive performance. ML model performance was evaluated using Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC), average precision (AP), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV, precision), negative predictive value (NPV), F1 score, Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC), balanced accuracy, false positive rate (FPR), false negative rate (FNR), and Brier score to allow a comprehensive evaluation of discrimination, classification performance, calibration, and overall predictive ability. Decision curve analysis (DCA) was performed separately for both HEP-FIB score and ML models to assess clinical utility. The HEP-FIB score demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance, achieving an AUC of 0.892 (95% CI: 0.859–0.925).At the optimal cutoff value (≥ 4), the score showed a sensitivity of 78%, specificity of 89%, and overall accuracy of 88%. HEP-FIB outperformed APRI (AUC 0.724), FIB-4 (AUC 0.654), and GPR (AUC 0.773) (all p < 0.001 by DeLong test). Bootstrap validation showed stable performance with an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.881. Calibration analysis showed good agreement between predicted and observed fibrosis probabilities, while DCA demonstrated superior net clinical benefit over default strategies. Among ML approaches, XGBoost achieved the best predictive performance, with an AUC of 0.914 (95% CI: 0.857–0.971), accuracy of 0.88, sensitivity of 0.72, specificity of 0.93, balanced accuracy of 0.83, and MCC of 0.74 in the validation dataset. The model demonstrated favorable calibration, evidenced by the low Brier score (0.095), together with reduced misclassification errors as reflected by low FPR (0.062) and FNR (0.275). elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)仍然是全球主要的健康负担。评估肝纤维化对于风险分层和指导治疗在慢性乙型肝炎中的治疗至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对382例慢性乙型肝炎患者进行了回顾性队列研究分析。该研究是一项单中心、内部验证的研究。该研究关注慢性乙型肝炎患者。
elements_zh.methods: 最小绝对值收缩和选择算子(LASSO)回归随后进行多变量逻辑回归用于识别纤维化的独立预测因子。我们开发并内部验证了基于常规实验室参数的简明评分系统HEP-FIB,并评估了机器学习(ML)模型在慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)患者中非侵入性预测显著肝纤维化的应用。
elements_zh.main_results: HEP-FIB评分表现出优异的诊断性能,实现了0.892的AUC(95% CI:0.859–0.925)。在最佳截断值(≥4)时,该评分显示出78%的灵敏度、89%的特异性和88%的总体准确性。HEP-FIB评分优于APRI(AUC 0.724)、FIB-4(AUC 0.654)和GPR(AUC 0.773)(所有p值均小于0.001,通过DeLong检验)。Bootstrap验证显示其性能稳定,校正乐观后的AUC为0.881。校准分析显示预测与观察到的纤维化概率之间有良好的一致性,而DCA显示其在默认策略上的净临床获益更优。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 基于血小板计数、肝功能参数和脂质生物标志物开发了一种新的HEP-FIB评分系统。集成机器学习模型在预测准确性方面略优于HEP-FIB评分。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: HEP-FIB评分在慢性乙型肝炎中显示出强大的诊断性能,用于识别显著肝纤维化,并在该回顾性、单中心队列研究研究中经过内部自举验证后优于传统的非侵入性纤维化评分。机器学习模型在诊断性能上仅显示出轻微的优势。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 在该评分被推荐用于常规临床应用之前,需要在独立且多样化的慢性乙型肝炎人群中进行外部验证。所提供的证据未报告研究结果的普遍适用性。

papers.abstract_zh: 慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)仍然是全球主要的健康负担。评估肝纤维化对于风险分层和指导治疗(抗病毒药物)治疗至关重要。肝活检作为纤维化分期的参考标准,具有侵入性且可能伴随潜在并发症,因此需要替代的非侵入性工具。现有的非侵入性纤维化评分系统在诊断准确性方面表现不一,且脂质在纤维化预测中的作用尚未被充分探索。我们开发并内部验证了一种基于常规实验室参数的简明评分系统HEP-FIB,并评估了机器学习(ML)模型在慢性乙型肝炎患者中非侵入性预测显著肝纤维化的性能。对382例慢性乙型肝炎患者的回顾性队列研究进行了分析。采用最小绝对值收缩和选择算子(LASSO)回归后进行多变量逻辑回归,以确定纤维化的独立预测因子。基于血小板计数、肝功能参数和脂质生物标志物,开发了一种新的HEP-FIB评分系统。使用受试者工作特征(ROC)曲线分析、自举内部验证和校准分析来评估诊断性能。将HEP-FIB的性能与已有的非侵入性指标进行比较,包括APRI、FIB-4和GPR。此外,构建并评估了十种机器学习算法的预测性能。通过受试者工作特征曲线下的面积(AUC)、平均精度(AP)、准确率、灵敏度、特异度、阳性预测值(PPV,精确度)、阴性预测值(NPV)、F1分数、马修斯相关系数(MCC)、平衡准确率、假阳性率(FPR)和假阴性率(FNR)以及布里尔分数(Brier score)来全面评估模型的区分能力、分类性能、校准和整体预测能力。分别对HEP-FIB评分系统和机器学习模型进行决策曲线分析(DCA),以评估其临床实用性。HEP-FIB评分系统表现出优异的诊断性能,其AUC为0.892(95% CI:0.859–0.925)。在最佳截断值(≥4)时,该评分系统显示出78%的灵敏度、89%的特异度和88%的总体准确率。HEP-FIB在内部自举验证后,在回顾性、单中心队列研究中表现出优于APRI(AUC 0.724)、FIB-4(AUC 0.654)和GPR(AUC 0.773)的性能(所有p值均小于0.001,通过DeLong检验)。自举验证显示其性能稳定,乐观校正后的AUC为0.881。校准分析显示预测的纤维化概率与实际观察结果之间有良好一致性,而DCA显示其相对于默认策略具有更高的净临床获益。在机器学习方法中,XGBoost在验证数据集中表现出最佳的预测性能,其AUC为0.914(95% CI:0.857–0.971),准确率为0.88,灵敏度为0.72,特异度为0.93,平衡准确率为0.83,MCC为0.74。该模型表现出良好的校准性能,这体现在较低的布里尔分数(0.095)以及较低的假阳性率(0.062)和假阴性率(0.275)所反映的误分类错误减少。DCA显示机器学习模型相较于测试所有和测试无策略具有更大的净临床获益。机器学习模型在预测性能方面相较于HEP-FIB评分系统表现出轻微优势。HEP-FIB在慢性乙型肝炎患者中表现出强大的诊断性能,能够识别显著肝纤维化,并在回顾性、单中心队列研究中优于传统非侵入性纤维化评分系统。集成机器学习模型在预测准确性方面略优于HEP-FIB评分系统。然而,在独立且多样化的慢性乙型肝炎人群中进行外部验证后,该评分系统才能被推荐用于常规临床实践。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)仍然是全球主要的健康负担。评估肝纤维化对于风险分层和指导治疗在慢性乙型肝炎中的治疗至关重要。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 对382例慢性乙型肝炎患者进行了回顾性队列研究分析。该研究是一项单中心、内部验证的研究。该研究关注慢性乙型肝炎患者。
analysis_zh.methods: 最小绝对值收缩和选择算子(LASSO)回归随后进行多变量逻辑回归用于识别纤维化的独立预测因子。我们开发并内部验证了基于常规实验室参数的简明评分系统HEP-FIB,并评估了机器学习(ML)模型在慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)患者中非侵入性预测显著肝纤维化的应用。
analysis_zh.main_results: HEP-FIB评分表现出优异的诊断性能,实现了0.892的AUC(95% CI:0.859–0.925)。在最佳截断值(≥4)时,该评分显示出78%的灵敏度、89%的特异性和88%的总体准确性。HEP-FIB评分优于APRI(AUC 0.724)、FIB-4(AUC 0.654)和GPR(AUC 0.773)(所有p值均小于0.001,通过DeLong检验)。Bootstrap验证显示其性能稳定,校正乐观后的AUC为0.881。校准分析显示预测与观察到的纤维化概率之间有良好的一致性,而DCA显示其在默认策略上的净临床获益更优。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 基于血小板计数、肝功能参数和脂质生物标志物开发了一种新的HEP-FIB评分系统。集成机器学习模型在预测准确性方面略优于HEP-FIB评分。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: HEP-FIB评分在慢性乙型肝炎中显示出强大的诊断性能,用于识别显著肝纤维化,并在该回顾性、单中心队列研究研究中经过内部自举验证后优于传统的非侵入性纤维化评分。机器学习模型在诊断性能上仅显示出轻微的优势。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 在该评分被推荐用于常规临床应用之前,需要在独立且多样化的慢性乙型肝炎人群中进行外部验证。所提供的证据未报告研究结果的普遍适用性。

papers.title: Expression of key factors in the TGF-β1/Smad2 pathway and their associations with clinicopathological characteristics and prognosis in HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma
papers.abstract: Abstract Background This study investigated the expression of TGF-β1 and Smad2 in hepatitis B virus (HBV)-associated hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and evaluated their associations with clinicopathological characteristics and prognosis. Methods In this prospective single-center cohort, 120 patients with HBV-associated HCC were enrolled between April 2022 and April 2024. TGF-β1 and Smad2 expression was assessed by immunohistochemistry in paired tumor and adjacent non-tumor tissues. Associations with clinicopathological characteristics and prognosis were examined using correlation analysis, logistic regression, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Follow-up lasted 12–36 months. Results TGF-β1 and Smad2 expression was significantly higher in tumor tissue than in paired adjacent non-tumor tissue (both P < 0.001). Higher expression was associated with poorer differentiation and more advanced stage ( P < 0.05). Patients with positive TGF-β1 or Smad2 expression had lower survival rates than those with negative expression. The AUCs for predicting death were 0.769 for TGF-β1, 0.756 for Smad2, and 0.892 for the combined model. Conclusions Elevated tumor expression of TGF-β1 and Smad2 is associated with aggressive clinicopathological features and poorer prognosis in HBV-associated HCC. Combined assessment of the two markers may improve prognostic discrimination compared with either marker alone; multicenter validation is warranted.

A prospective single-center cohort of 120 patients was enrolled between April 2022 and April 2024. TGF-β1 and Smad2 expression was assessed using immunohistochemistry in paired tumor and non-tumor tissues, and their associations were analyzed with statistical methods. Results showed significantly higher expression of both markers in tumor tissue compared to non-tumor tissue, with higher expression linked to poorer differentiation and more advanced stages. The study's findings may contribute to improved prognostic assessment and guide targeted therapeutic strategies. However, the single-center design and limited follow-up period may restrict generalizability, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 本研究探讨了TGF-β1和Smad2在乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)相关肝细胞癌(HCC)中的表达,并评估其与临床病理特征和预后的关系。方法 在这项前瞻性单中心研究中,于2022年4月至2024年4月期间纳入了120例乙型肝炎病毒相关肝细胞癌患者。通过免疫组化法检测配对肿瘤组织和相邻非肿瘤组织中TGF-β1和Smad2的表达。采用相关分析、逻辑回归、Kaplan-Meier生存分析和受试者工作特征(ROC)分析评估其与临床病理特征和预后的关系。随访时间为12–36个月。结果 肿瘤组织中TGF-β1和Smad2的表达显著高于配对的相邻非肿瘤组织(两者P < 0.001)。高表达与较差的分化程度和更晚期的分期相关(P < 0.05)。TGF-β1或Smad2表达阳性患者死亡率低于表达阴性者。预测死亡的AUC分别为TGF-β1为0.769,Smad2为0.756,联合模型为0.892。结论 乙型肝炎病毒相关肝细胞癌中肿瘤组织TGF-β1和Smad2的高表达与更具侵袭性的临床病理特征和较差的预后相关。与单独使用任一标志物相比,联合评估这两个标志物可能提高预后判别的能力;需要多中心验证。

strengthening collaboration, preparedness & response Home Publications and data European standards of prevention and care: Module on antenatal screening for HIV, hepatitis B and syphilis Publications and data European standards of prevention and care: Module on antenatal screening for HIV, hepatitis B and syphilis Operational support 24 September 2026 The global community has committed to eliminating vertical transmission of HIV, hepatitis B virus (HBV) and syphilis as a public health priority. This global commitment encourages countries to provide the most effective, high-quality and person-centred care available to pregnant and breastfeeding people, aiming to ensure a generation born free of HIV, syphilis and HBV. Antenatal screening (ANS) programmes, including universal screening for transmissible infections, aim to ensure optimal parent and child health for all including population groups identified as vulnerable to vertical transmission in line with the overarching objective of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) of leaving no one behind. In the European Union/European Economic Area (EU/EEA), the number of births was 3.67 million in 2023. Data on the annual number of people living with HIV giving birth are not available at European level. However, data on vertical transmission of HIV and syphilis are available. In 2024, 196 newly diagnosed HIV infections in the EU/EEA were reported as resulting from vertical transmission. Of these, 75% (147 cases) were among migrants, defined as people whose country of origin was outside the reporting country. In 2024, there were 140 reports of confirmed congenital syphilis in 28 reporting EU/EEA countries, corresponding to an overall EU/EEA notification rate of 4.7 per 100 000 live births. Of the 63 cases with available data, the maternal country of birth differed from the reporting country in 17 (27%) cases. From 2023 to 2024, there was nearly a doubling of congenital syphilis cases reported by EU/EEA countries. For hepatitis B, data on transmission were complete for 24% of the acute hepatitis B cases reported in 2023 in the EU/EEA countries, of which only 1% were due to vertical transmission. Data on transmission was complete for 9% of chronic hepatitis B cases. For the 1 421 newly diagnosed chronic cases with complete information, vertical transmission was the most common route of transmission (39%) but the majority (91%) were classified as being imported meaning vertical transmission occurred in countries of origin and not in the reporting country. Publication file European Standards of prevention and care: Module on Antenatal Screening for HIV, hepatitis B and syphilis English (1.44 MB - PDF) Download What are standards of care for HIV? The standards of care (SoC) for HIV define the expected, or desired, quality of prevention, treatment, and care forpeople at risk of HIV acquisition or living with HIV. The standards are based on a scientific rationale, as well as the responsibilities of each stakeholder and ensure that people receive appropriate, high-quality prevention and care that aligns with the most up-to-date medical knowledge and ethical standards. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) in partnership with the European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS) have developed standards of care in the areas of HIV testing, pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), antenatal screening, commencement of ART, and HIV and co-morbidities (add links to SoC modules). Each standard is based on the following structure: 1. Brief description of the rationale for the standard. 2. Quality statements describing best practice based on current guidelines, evidence, and expert opinion. 3. related measurable and auditable outcome indicators used to assess the quality and effectiveness of the services. 4. Numeric values for defined targets. The standards are person-centred in their approach with a specific focus on being equitable, non-discriminatory, relevant, appropriate, and accessible for people at risk of or living with HIV. analysis.brief_en: The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) and the European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS) have developed standards of care for antenatal screening of HIV, hepatitis B, and syphilis. These standards aim to prevent vertical transmission and ensure equitable, high-quality care for pregnant and breastfeeding individuals. In 2024, 196 newly diagnosed HIV infections in the EU/EEA were reported as resulting from vertical transmission, with 75% among migrants. For hepatitis B, only 1% of acute cases in 2023 were due to vertical transmission, and 39% of chronic cases had vertical transmission as the most common route, though 91% were classified as imported. The report highlights the importance of comprehensive data collection and the need for improved reporting mechanisms to better understand and address vertical transmission risks. The standards are based on scientific rationale, best practices, and ethical considerations, with a focus on accessibility and non-discrimination.

Addressing a side event of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York, organised by the UN Group of Friends to Eliminate Hepatitis, Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava highlighted India’s comprehensive, people-centred response across prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment and care. The Health Secretary said India has strengthened interventions across the continuum from antenatal screening and Hepatitis B immunisation to free diagnosis and treatment, safe blood transfusion services, counselling and rehabilitation support for people who inject drugs. She emphasised the importance of sustained global cooperation, equitable access to prevention, testing and treatment, and stronger health systems to accelerate progress towards the 2030 targets. news.title_zh: 印度承诺到2030年消除乙型肝炎和丙型肝炎作为公共卫生威胁,卫生部长称 - 新闻快报
news.source_body_en: India has reaffirmed its commitment to eliminating Hepatitis B and C as public health threats by 2030, as stated by Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava during a side event of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York. The commitment includes strengthening interventions across the continuum of prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment, and care, such as antenatal screening, Hepatitis B immunisation, free diagnosis and treatment, safe blood transfusion services, and support for people who inject drugs. The Health Secretary also stressed the importance of global cooperation, equitable access to prevention, testing, and treatment, and stronger health systems to achieve these targets. While no specific case, death, or exposure counts were reported, the response is ongoing and involves a comprehensive strategy. The commitment reflects a long-term public health initiative rather than an immediate outbreak or incident.
news.content_zh: 印度重申了到2030年消除乙型肝炎和丙型肝炎作为公共卫生威胁的承诺,正如联合卫生部长Punya Salila Srivastava在纽约联合国大会第81届会议期间的一次边会中所强调的。该承诺包括在整个预防、筛查、诊断、治疗和治疗过程中加强干预措施,例如产前筛查、乙型肝炎疫苗接种、免费诊断和治疗、安全的输血服务以及对注射毒品者的咨询和康复支持。卫生部长还强调了全球合作、预防、检测和治疗的公平获取以及更强健的卫生系统对于实现这些目标的重要性。虽然没有报告具体的病例、死亡或暴露数量,但应对工作正在进行中,并涉及全面的策略。该承诺反映了长期的公共卫生倡议,而不是立即的暴发或事件。
news.summary_zh: 印度重申了到2030年消除乙型肝炎和丙型肝炎作为公共卫生威胁的承诺,正如联合卫生部长Punya Salila Srivastava在纽约联合国大会第81届会议期间的一次边会中所强调的。该承诺包括在整个预防、筛查、诊断、治疗和治疗过程中加强干预措施,例如产前筛查、乙型肝炎疫苗接种、免费诊断和治疗、安全的输血服务以及对注射毒品者的咨询和康复支持。卫生部长还强调了全球合作、预防、检测和治疗的公平获取以及更强健的卫生系统对于实现这些目标的重要性。虽然没有报告具体的病例、死亡或暴露数量,但应对工作正在进行中,并涉及全面的策略。该承诺反映了长期的公共卫生倡议,而不是立即的暴发或事件。

analysis_zh.time: 印度重申了到2030年抗击病毒性肝炎并消除乙型肝炎和丙型肝炎作为公共卫生威胁的承诺(N1)。活动日期未明确说明,但该承诺是在纽约联合国大会第81届会议期间作出的(N2)。
analysis_zh.location_and_population: 该承诺涉及印度的全体人口,重点是加强预防、筛查、诊断、治疗和治疗过程中的干预措施(N3)。
analysis_zh.event: 印度重申了到2030年消除乙型肝炎和丙型肝炎作为公共卫生威胁的承诺,正如联合卫生部长Punya Salila Srivastava在联合国大会边会上所强调的(N2)。这是一个确认的承诺,而不是暴发或事件(N1)。
analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 卫生部长强调了在从产前筛查和乙型肝炎疫苗接种到免费诊断和治疗、安全输血服务以及对注射毒品者的咨询和康复支持等整个干预链条中加强措施(N3)。这些措施旨在减轻乙型肝炎和丙型肝炎的负担,但没有报告具体的病例、死亡或暴露数量(N1,N2,N3,N4)。
analysis_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 该承诺包括加强干预措施,并强调持续的全球合作、预防、检测和治疗的公平获取以及更强健的卫生系统(N3,N4)。应对工作正在进行中,尚未解决,且未提及当前状态或调查(N1,N2,N3,N4)。

news.content_title: Molecular basis and clinical significance of the high-risk phenotype of hepatitis B virus genotype C
news.content: Home Article Highlight | 24-Sep-2026 Molecular basis and clinical significance of the high-risk phenotype of hepatitis B virus genotype C Xia & He Publishing Inc. Facebook X LinkedIn WeChat Bluesky Message WhatsApp Email image: HBV genotype C represents a clinically relevant high-risk form of chronic HBV infection. It is generally associated with delayed HBeAg seroconversion, persistent viral replication, more active hepatic inflammation, faster fibrosis progression, and a higher risk of HCC. Importantly, this risk may persist even after effective antiviral suppression, especially in patients with advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis. The high-risk phenotype of genotype C appears to be related to its viral sequence background, enrichment of BCP/preC/HBx-related variants, altered HBeAg expression, immune dysregulation, HBx-related oncogenic signaling, and HBV integration-associated genomic instability. Although these mechanisms are not exclusive to genotype C, they may be more clinically relevant in genotype C infection because of the prolonged replication phase, enrichment of high-risk viral variants, and greater cumulative inflammatory and oncogenic injury. In clinical practice, genotype C should be viewed as a risk-enhancing virological factor rather than a stand-alone determinant of treatment or surveillance decisions. Combining genotype information with viral mutations, fibrosis stage, cirrhosis status, treatment response, and emerging biomarkers may help refine long-term risk assessment and surveillance planning for patients with chronic hepatitis B. view more Credit: Lei Sang, Tao Shen HBV genotype C is common in East Asia and linked to cirrhosis and HCC. It features persistent replication, delayed HBeAg seroconversion, active inflammation, and high HCC risk. Key drivers include BCP A1762T/G1764A, preC G1896A, abnormal HBx, and viral integration. This review summarises the molecular features, pathogenic mechanisms, and clinical implications, and discusses genotype‐informed risk stratification. Introduction CHB progression varies widely. Viral factors, especially genotype and mutations, are key determinants. Genotype C is associated with poorer outcomes. BCP/preC mutations produce high replication with low HBeAg expression; HBx dysfunction and viral integration contribute to inflammation and hepatocarcinogenesis. Virological Features Distribution: Predominant in Asia/Oceania. Subgenotypes: C1 (Southeast Asia), C2 (China, Korea, Japan), C3/C4 (Oceania). Mixed infection may increase replication and inflammation. Genome: ~3.2 kb circular DNA with four overlapping ORFs. In genotype C, sequence background influences emergence of regulatory mutations. PreC and BCP are critical for HBeAg expression and replication. A1762T/G1764A is more frequent in genotype C. Nucleotide 1858 (C in genotype C, T in B) affects G1896A stability. Key mutations: BCP A1762T/G1764A: Reduces HBeAg, enhances pgRNA and replication; causes HBx K130M/V131I. Associated with increased HCC risk, stronger in genotype C. preC G1896A: Stop codon, abolishes HBeAg. Constrained by ε stem‐loop; less frequent and later in genotype C. Marker of HBeAg‐negative CHB. Synergy: Co‐occurrence of BCP and preC mutations increases cirrhosis/HCC risk. Quasispecies: Viral diversity under immune pressure promotes accumulation of high‐risk variants. Molecular Mechanisms HBeAg loss and immune dysregulation: Reduced HBeAg disrupts immune tolerance, causing persistent ineffective inflammation, repeated hepatocyte injury, and fibrosis. HBx/BCP variants: Activate Wnt/β‐catenin (via APC/GSK3β, SFRP1/5 repression) and JAK/STAT3 (via ROS, mitochondrial dysfunction). K130M/V131I and truncated HBx enhance oncogenic signalling. Genotype C justifies strict surveillance adherence and active risk reassessment, not automatic interval shortening. It is not a single treatment indication but may support earlier reassessment in borderline cases. Perspectives Most evidence treats genotype C as one category; subgenotype C2 data are limited. Genotype C should be viewed as a risk‐enhancing factor, not a stand‐alone determinant. Combining genotype with viral mutations, fibrosis, cirrhosis, treatment response, and emerging biomarkers may refine long‐term risk assessment and surveillance. news.content: Latest Celebrity K-Pop Drama Movie Culture K-Beauty Latest Celebrity K-Pop Drama Movie Culture K-Beauty Home Culture "Hepatitis B: Active treatment recommended when viral load is high even if liver enzyme levels are normal" By Jongho, Jang Published 2026-09-23 10:02 Share this article X Facebook Copy Copy URL copied. File photo courtesy of Pixabay [Sportschosun, Jang Jong-ho] For years, liver enzyme levels were one of the key criteria for determining antiviral treatment for patients with hepatitis B. However, treatment strategies are changing בעקבות research showing that even patients with normal liver enzyme levels face a higher risk of liver damage and liver cancer if they have a high hepatitis B viral load. Yoo Jeong-ju, a professor of gastroenterology at Soonchunhyang University Bucheon Hospital, said, "Recently, the treatment of chronic hepatitis B has shifted away from waiting until inflammation develops in the liver. The focus is now on suppressing viral replication early to prevent cirrhosis and liver cancer." Hepatitis B is caused by the hepatitis B virus infecting liver cells. Most adults who become acutely infected recover naturally, but infections acquired during the newborn or infant period, or while a person is immunocompromised, can persist for more than six months and develop into chronic hepatitis B. Once the disease becomes chronic, inflammation and fibrosis gradually progress in the liver and can lead to cirrhosis, liver failure and hepatocellular carcinoma. The number of people with chronic hepatitis B in South Korea is estimated at approximately 1.2 million. Although the diagnosis rate is relatively high at about 83%, only 22.2% actually receive treatment, leaving a substantial gap between diagnosis and treatment. Approximately 60% of liver cancer deaths in South Korea are reportedly attributable to hepatitis B, making early diagnosis and management crucial. Acute hepatitis B infection can cause fatigue, loss of appetite, a low-grade fever, nausea, jaundice and dark urine. Chronic hepatitis B, however, is often asymptomatic until the liver has sustained considerable damage. The most common route of infection is vertical transmission from an infected mother to her child at birth. It can also spread through blood transfusions, exposure to contaminated needles, invasive procedures, sexual contact, and exposure to blood or bodily fluids among family members. It is not transmitted through ordinary meals, hugging, sneezing or other casual contact. The 2026 revised clinical guidelines redefine chronic hepatitis B as a viral infectious disease rather than an inflammatory liver disease. They also shift the main criterion for treatment decisions from liver enzyme levels, particularly ALT, to viral load, measured by HBV DNA. As a result, moderate viremia, which was often monitored rather than actively treated when liver enzyme levels were normal, has been added as a new treatment category. Moderate viremia refers to a blood viral load ranging from 2,000 to 108 IU/mL. A recent large-scale cohort study in South Korea found that patients in this range had a higher risk of developing hepatocellular carcinoma than patients with high viremia, defined as an HBV DNA level of 108 IU/mL or higher. An interim analysis of a joint randomized clinical trial in South Korea and Taiwan also confirmed that early antiviral treatment substantially reduced the risk of serious clinical events, including liver cancer, decompensated liver disease and death. Patients with a viral load below 2,000 IU/mL, who do not face a high risk of liver damage, are monitored through regular follow-up examinations. Active antiviral treatment is recommended for patients with high viremia who have risk factors such as older age, a family history of liver cancer or liver fibrosis. The standard treatment for chronic hepatitis B is to suppress viral replication with oral antiviral medications such as tenofovir and entecavir. Patients who achieve a complete cure by eliminating the hepatitis B virus remain rare. The practical treatment goal is to suppress HBV DNA to undetectable levels over the long term, thereby preventing the progression of liver inflammation and fibrosis and reducing the risk of cirrhosis, liver failure and liver cancer. Even when the virus is well controlled with antiviral treatment, patients whose liver fibrosis or cirrhosis has already progressed remain at risk of developing liver cancer. Accordingly, patients with chronic hepatitis B should undergo liver cancer surveillance, including liver ultrasonography and blood tests, every six months. Family members and household contacts of patients with hepatitis B should undergo tests for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and surface antibody (anti-HBs) to determine whether they are infected and whether they have immunity. Those who are infected should undergo liver enzyme and liver fibrosis tests to assess the extent of liver damage, with liver ultrasonography or a biopsy performed when necessary. Those who are not infected but lack antibodies can receive vaccination. Patients already diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B should avoid excessive alcohol consumption and be cautious about taking dietary supplements or folk remedies whose efficacy and safety have not been established. In particular, abruptly stopping antiviral medication without a doctor's instructions can cause rapid viral reactivation and worsen hepatitis, making consistent medication adherence and regular medical appointments important. When hepatitis B progresses to cirrhosis or liver cancer, close multidisciplinary cooperation among internal medicine, surgery, radiology and radiation oncology is essential. Soonchunhyang University Bucheon Hospital has a well-established multidisciplinary care system that enables efficient coordination among departments and prompt treatment. With additional liver transplant specialists recently joining the hospital, minimally invasive procedures such as laparoscopic and robotic surgery are expected to expand, allowing the hospital to provide more patient-centered care. Professor Yoo Jeong-ju said, "Hepatitis B is a disease whose risks of cirrhosis and liver cancer can be greatly reduced through early detection and appropriate treatment and management." She emphasized, "If you have never been tested for hepatitis B, it is advisable to check whether you are infected and whether you have antibodies through a health screening or other examination. Patients with hepatitis B should also undergo regular testing so they do not miss the appropriate time to begin treatment." analysis.brief_en: The article discusses updated treatment guidelines for chronic hepatitis B in South Korea, emphasizing the shift from relying on liver enzyme levels to monitoring viral load, specifically HBV DNA levels, for treatment decisions. This change is based on research showing that patients with normal liver enzymes but high viral load face a higher risk of liver damage and cancer. The guidelines recommend early antiviral treatment for those with moderate viremia (2,000 to 108 IU/mL) and high viral load, particularly in individuals with risk factors such as older age or a family history of liver cancer. The focus is on long-term suppression of the virus to prevent progression to cirrhosis, liver failure, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Patients with chronic hepatitis B are advised to undergo regular liver cancer surveillance, including ultrasonography and blood tests, every six months. Additionally, family members and household contacts should be tested for HBsAg and anti-HBs to determine infection status and immunity. The article highlights the importance of consistent medication adherence and avoiding abrupt discontinuation of antiviral therapy. It also mentions the role of multidisciplinary care in managing advanced stages of the disease, such as cirrhosis or liver cancer.

news.content_zh: 本文讨论了韩国最新的慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)治疗指南,强调从依赖肝酶水平转向监测病毒载量,特别是乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)DNA水平,以决定抗病毒治疗(治疗)。这一转变基于研究显示,肝酶水平正常但病毒载量高的患者面临更高的肝损伤和肝癌风险。指南建议对病毒载量中等(2,000至108 IU/mL)或高病毒载量的患者,尤其是具有风险因素(如年龄较大或有肝癌家族史)的人群,尽早开始抗病毒治疗。重点在于长期抑制病毒,以防止进展为肝硬化、肝衰竭和肝细胞癌。患有慢性乙型肝炎的患者被建议每六个月进行一次肝癌筛查,包括超声检查和血液检测。此外,家庭成员和密切接触者应接受HBsAg和抗-HBs检测,以确定感染状态和免疫力。文章强调了持续服药的重要性,并避免突然中断抗病毒治疗。它还提到了多学科团队在管理疾病晚期阶段(如肝硬化或肝癌)中的作用。

news.content: Hepatitis B is a disease in which the hepatitis B virus, HBV, causes inflammation of the liver. If it becomes chronic, it can lead to cirrhosis or liver cancer, so patients should, when necessary, manage the condition by taking antiviral medication consistently. In particular, stopping antiviral medication on one’s own during treatment can allow the virus to replicate again and worsen hepatitis, so caution is required. In severe cases, it can progress to liver failure with a rapid decline in liver function. Health Chosun summarized a case from the Korea Medical Dispute Mediation and Arbitration Agency’s mediation records in which a patient being treated for hepatitis B stopped antiviral medication and took herbal medicine, after which her liver function deteriorated and she died. ◇Case overview A, a woman in her 50s, had been taking antiviral medication for chronic hepatitis B since around 2009. From May 2019 she took the antiviral drug Viread tablets, and in August of the same year she received an in-person consultation at B Korean Medicine Clinic and was prescribed Saenggan-tang. For about four months thereafter, she received additional prescriptions for Saenggan-tang via telephone consultations. In November 2019 A stopped taking Viread. Afterwards her liver enzyme levels rose and she experienced indigestion, nausea, and fatigue. In December of that year, the indicators used to assess liver cell damage, AST, GOT, rose to 240 IU/L and ALT, GPT, rose to 495 IU/L. During a January 2020 telephone consultation, medical staff at B Korean Medicine Clinic, having noted this condition, advised A to seek hospital care and to be admitted to a higher-level hospital. However, about five days later A’s ALT rose to 1000 IU/L and jaundice appeared, and she was admitted to another hospital. Despite receiving antiviral treatment, about a week later she developed hepatic encephalopathy with decreased consciousness. She was transferred to another hospital to consider the possibility of a liver transplant, but liver function did not recover, and after continued treatment at several hospitals she ultimately died. ◇Family, “Due to herbal medicine and stopping medication” vs Clinic, “No evidence Saenggan-tang caused side effects” The family argued that the herbal medicine’s toxicity and the discontinuation of antiviral medication contributed to A’s rapid deterioration. They also said that although A complained of abnormal symptoms, appropriate measures were not taken and the opportunity for timely treatment was missed. By contrast, B Korean Medicine Clinic denied there was any basis to conclude that Saenggan-tang caused A’s rapid deterioration and death. ◇"Causality not confirmed... explanations and monitoring were insufficient" The Mediation Agency judged that it was difficult to view the mere prescription of Saenggan-tang to A as inappropriate, and that a clear causal relationship between Saenggan-tang and acute-on-chronic liver failure was not established. Because B Korean Medicine Clinic knew that A planned to stop the antiviral medication she had been taking for a long time, the agency said the clinic should have sufficiently explained the possibility of viral reactivation and hepatitis worsening after stopping the medication, the need for ongoing testing, and similar risks. It also found that although A reported indigestion, nausea, and fatigue and her liver enzyme levels rose significantly after stopping the antiviral medication, the clinic’s follow-up observation was inadequate, for example by not recommending an in-person examination or additional testing. However, the agency found insufficient evidence that B Korean Medicine Clinic directly encouraged the discontinuation of the antiviral medication, and it was also difficult to conclude that the inadequate explanations and follow-up observation directly caused A’s liver failure and death. The agency noted that A herself did not immediately accept the recommendation for hospitalization, which also contributed to the missed opportunity for appropriate treatment. In the end, the Mediation Agency concluded that B Korean Medicine Clinic did not adequately fulfill its duty to explain and to monitor progress, thereby infringing on A’s right to choose treatment and opportunity for early treatment, and proposed a settlement awarding the bereaved family 20 million won in compensation. Both parties accepted this proposal and the mediation was concluded. ◇Do not stop hepatitis B medication on your own... be cautious with herbal medicine and supplements Patients with chronic hepatitis B should not stop antiviral medication on their own. Antiviral drugs suppress viral replication to reduce liver damage, and stopping them can allow the virus to increase again and worsen hepatitis. Decisions about stopping medication should be made with medical staff based on liver condition, viral load, and treatment response, and after stopping medication the virus and liver enzyme levels should be regularly monitored. When taking herbal medicine or dietary supplements, it is also advisable to inform medical staff that you have liver disease and to tell them what medications you are currently taking. Not all herbal medicines or supplements are harmful to the liver, but some ingredients can cause liver damage, and products that combine multiple ingredients can make it difficult to identify the cause if problems arise. If you experience unusually severe fatigue, loss of appetite, persistent nausea, yellowing of the skin and the whites of the eyes indicating jaundice, or darkening of the urine, you should seek medical care as these may indicate worsening liver function.
